protocol.selection_order: All scope exclusions by registry_order, then all exceptions by counselor_programme_id; resume by audit_population plus counselor_programme_id.
protocol.population_start: Current normalized data/registry/programmes.csv; upstream DUO/RIO population is out of scope.
protocol.confirmed_meaning: Supports only the facts and decision within audit_scope. For no-defensible-ucr-match, confirmation applies only to external-programme basis; UCR reassessment remains pending.
protocol.outdated_rule: Requires dated evidence establishing that the original decision was supportable and that a later change superseded it. Record temporal uncertainty explicitly when historical evidence cannot distinguish incorrect from outdated.
protocol.resolved_external_curriculum_action: Normally reassess-exception: an externally reconstructable comparator alone does not establish UCR feasibility.
protocol.reprocess_as_comparison_rule: Recommend only when comparison eligibility is independently established; do not infer it merely from resolved external evidence.
protocol.incomplete_batches: Keep pending cases explicit without audit_finding; never count pending cases as audited.
protocol.final_reconciliation: Every excluded target and every current exception must have exactly one completed audit entry per audit_population; report missing in-scope records separately.

reconciliation_evidence.exception_type_check: Read all 140 exception canonical JSON records directly; verified their IDs and recordStatus and inventoried exception.type only. This is population enumeration, not exception research.
reconciliation_evidence.comparison_count_basis: Current generated review index, with its complete ID set reconciled to both registry scope and canonical filenames; comparison contents were not audited.

b15_guide_378.title: UvA official current weighted study guide
b15_guide_378.locator: Selected curriculum page 39547, compulsory/common and selected path nodes; years 1–3
b15_guide_378.fact: Current selected positive-credit template closes 60/60/60; zero-credit compulsory formation is separate. Alternative specialization nodes are mutually exclusive; API aggregate 108/90 is not a single pathway. Select only Arabic Studies, not Middle Eastern Studies; retain current valid selection. Language 1/2 precede 3/4; first-year Arabic preparation precedes communicating/literary discourse. Compulsory abroad 30 is approved Cairo study, not free profiling. Zero-credit diagnostic test and tutoring are mandatory without increasing 180. Current Arabic Studies thesis is 12.

b15_guide_379.title: UvA official current weighted study guide
b15_guide_379.locator: Selected curriculum page 40339, compulsory/common and selected path nodes; years 1–3
b15_guide_379.fact: Current selected positive-credit template closes 60/60/60; zero-credit compulsory formation is separate. Retain the English curriculum variant, not both language tests; rc-0047 merged Dutch/English institutional variants. Field School 1 precedes Field School 2; thesis requires successful completion of all compulsory first- and second-year courses. Current year placement is catalogue-controlled. ACASA collaboration is not automatically a current joint award; official joint degree is announced for 2027–2028.

b15_guide_390.title: UvA official current weighted study guide
b15_guide_390.locator: Selected curriculum page 39880, compulsory/common and selected path nodes; years 1–3
b15_guide_390.fact: Current selected positive-credit template closes 60/60/60; zero-credit compulsory formation is separate. Required abroad 30 is distinct from genuine free 30. Thesis requires positive BSA, completed first year and at least 54 EC of second-year work; complete year two meets the weighted gate. Duitslandstudies branding and diploma Duitse Taal en Cultuur retain the same current registry target.

b15_guide_398.title: UvA official current weighted study guide
b15_guide_398.locator: Selected curriculum page 40799, compulsory/common and selected path nodes; years 1–3
b15_guide_398.fact: Current selected positive-credit template closes 60/60/60; zero-credit compulsory formation is separate. Required abroad 30 is separate from genuine free 30. Full-time exchange follows at least 54 first-year EC and attendance of second-year semester one; part-time exchange is third year at earliest. Graduation project 12 and French-writing prerequisites remain; retain current courses despite differences in prospective versus current timetable order.

b15_guide_403.title: UvA official current weighted study guide
b15_guide_403.locator: Selected curriculum page 40330, compulsory/common and selected path nodes; years 1–3
b15_guide_403.fact: Current selected positive-credit template closes 60/60/60; zero-credit compulsory formation is separate. Ordinary regular-language-prepared path is selected. Adapted entry with one prior classical language requires an authorized compensated curriculum, not extra stacked bridging credits. Thesis requires all compulsory first- and second-year courses passed. Ancient languages are subject/read languages unless instruction evidence establishes otherwise. ACASA joint degree and RIO change are future 2027–2028 changes, not backdated to this current 2026 guide.

b15_guide_404.title: UvA official current weighted study guide
b15_guide_404.locator: Selected curriculum page 39356, compulsory/common and selected path nodes; years 1–3
b15_guide_404.fact: Current selected positive-credit template closes 60/60/60; zero-credit compulsory formation is separate. Alternative specialization nodes are mutually exclusive; API aggregate 108/90 is not a single pathway. Select only Jewish Studies and Hebrew; do not stack Middle Eastern Studies. Weighted allocation 180 does not resolve the missing compulsory abroad prerequisite or current host conflicts. Ulpan remains 6 EC: guide and objectives indicate B2 while English title says C1; do not treat title as verified achievement. Conditional five-course home alternative requires explicit authorization and current weights/gates; it is not silently substituted.

b15_guide_408.title: UvA official current weighted study guide
b15_guide_408.locator: Selected curriculum page 40875, compulsory/common and selected path nodes; years 1–3
b15_guide_408.fact: Current selected positive-credit template closes 60/60/60; zero-credit compulsory formation is separate. Italian 5 requires 1–4; abroad requires all six language courses, first-year 60 and year-two semester-one attendance. Full-time placement can meet this sequence. Part-time exchange begins no earlier than year three. All compulsory courses, including year-three Good Italy/Bad Italy, must be passed before thesis. Required abroad 30 and thesis 12 are separate from genuinely free 30. English course titles alone do not establish English instruction.

b15_guide_411.title: UvA official current weighted study guide
b15_guide_411.locator: Selected curriculum page 39692, compulsory/common and selected path nodes; years 1–3
b15_guide_411.fact: Current selected positive-credit template closes 60/60/60; zero-credit compulsory formation is separate. Broad Linguistics is the least specialized matching route; Sign Language Linguistics stays an alternative. Catalan appears first but has no course membership in this catalogue snapshot; Czech is the first complete eligible Language X sequence, 1–4 each 6 with preceding course passed. English teaching of Czech courses does not add Czech to programme instruction. Specialization Linguistics 6 is one compulsory unit before thesis. Tentative themes are not formal graduation tracks. Thesis requires Intro Linguistics, positive BSA, Linguistic Theories and Specialization passed.

b16_guide_416.title: UvA 2026–2027 weighted Musicology (Muziekwetenschap) curriculum
b16_guide_416.locator: Published curriculum nodes and course weights via official public catalogue API used by its client; one selected study path
b16_guide_416.fact: The retained Cognitive and Computational Musicology route has a nominal current guide allocation of 60/60/60, but Musical Celebrities (115221386Y, 6 EC) appears in both years two and three: the distinct credited units total only 174. Current 2026 transition rules replace earlier 3-EC methods with 6-EC methods and make Musical Celebrities a replacement for older project/portfolio requirements. The prospective table still shows the older 3-EC methods and generic 6-EC second-year space. These cannot be combined into a certified new-entry 180-EC path. The stored common aggregate conceals membership, and the exception’s 42-EC genuinely open claim conflicts with its stored free 36. Independently, English-taught compulsory/selected courses and omitted zero-credit diagnostic/tutoring formation establish current corrections.

b16_guide_419.title: UvA 2026–2027 weighted Modern Greek Language and Culture (Nieuwgriekse taal en cultuur) curriculum
b16_guide_419.locator: Published curriculum nodes and course weights via official public catalogue API used by its client; one selected study path
b16_guide_419.fact: The current weighted Greek programme closes at 60/60/60, including abroad 30 and thesis 12; it resolves the misleading 6-EC abroad label in the prospective table. Compulsory diagnostic/tutoring formation at zero EC is omitted. Current course offerings establish English and Modern Greek teaching alongside Dutch, so NLD-only normalization is incomplete. The introduction explicitly allows an adapted home programme for students who cannot or do not wish to go abroad; mobility is not universal across every permitted path.

b16_guide_428.title: UvA 2026–2027 weighted Religiewetenschappen curriculum
b16_guide_428.locator: Published curriculum nodes and course weights via official public catalogue API used by its client; one selected study path
b16_guide_428.fact: The full 180-EC Religious Studies curriculum is supported, but the compulsory first-year restricted disciplinary package of 24 EC has no concrete stored selection. Anthropology is the first complete package in current catalogue order: Introduction to Anthropology 12 plus Current Debates 1: Connecting Worlds 12. This is a first-year choice package, not a separately invented graduation track. Its English-taught courses and compulsory English Secrets of the West establish ENG alongside NLD. Diagnostic/tutoring zero-credit formation is omitted.

b16_guide_429.fact: The retained Danish route’s positive-credit requirements close 60/60/60, including required selected abroad 30, translation 6 and graduation project 12. Diagnostic/tutoring at zero EC is missing. Danish 1 is explicitly Danish-taught while several later shared/course summaries remain Dutch; the programme language statement also includes the language of the degree. b16_guide_437.title: UvA 2026–2027 weighted Theatre Studies (Theaterwetenschap) curriculum

cases.programme_display_name: Religion, Politics and Society (Religie, Politiek en Samenleving)
cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The defining curriculum is religious studies: a full first year studying Judaism, Islam, Christianity, Hinduism, Buddhism, sacred texts, religious practices, theology, sociology and anthropology of religion; a further 45 EC of second-year work in philosophy of religious studies, spirituality, religious identity, migration, ritual and religious media; at least two 15-EC religion-based thematic modules; and an independent religion-politics-society final work. Even with the 30 EC genuinely free minor space, 150 EC remains in religious-studies and religion-linked practice, methods, modules and thesis. UCR lacks a dedicated course in the study of religion, religious traditions, theology or religion-specific research methods, let alone a coherent 24-course religious-studies progression. A programme in politics, philosophy and sociology could study surrounding social questions but would omit the target’s defining religion curriculum and would misrepresent a nearest academic match.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The defining 120 EC in years one and two is chemistry and laboratory centred: analytical, organic and inorganic chemistry; molecular structure and bonding; thermodynamics, quantum mechanics and physics; successive chemical synthesis and analysis laboratories. In year three, at least 12 EC of chemistry electives and a 12-EC independent chemistry research internship/report remain required. Although 27 EC can be freely chosen, UCR lacks a chemistry gateway and any stand-alone introductory or advanced organic, inorganic, analytical, physical or synthetic chemistry sequence. A 24-course UCR route using biology, geoscience, statistics and programming would have too little chemistry and would misrepresent the programme’s academic core.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The prospective year pages total 60+60+60=180 EC. Year one consists of twelve required 5-EC linguistics and supporting methods/AI courses; zero-credit academic language and mentoring entries are excluded. Year two consists of six required 5-EC linguistics courses (30 EC) and two required 15-EC arts minors. The selected supplementary linguistics minor 1 uses the first three listed 5-EC courses (language developmental disorders, language and thought, social interaction); minor 2 lists exactly three 5-EC courses (speech/voice/hearing, Dutch as a second language and Python). The prospective page mistakenly labels each individual supplementary-minor heading 30 EC, whereas its prose requires two minors of 15 EC each and the adopted 2026–27 OER independently states a 30-EC total year-two minor. Treating the headings as additive would give 90 EC for year two, contradicting both sources and the programme total. The ordinary, non-abroad prospective year three includes 5 EC language proficiency, 10 EC professional development, 5 EC language norms, a 10-EC research thesis and 30 EC genuinely free space; the abroad variant is not combined. The 2026–27 OER names different year-three taught major units (Pragmatics and History of Dutch) from the indicative 2029–30 webpage (Language proficiency and Language norms). This is a difference between distinct academic years, not evidence that 2029–30 has a guaranteed adopted curriculum. The selected route follows the prospective year pages, and the formal OER is cited only for the second-year 30-EC minor-space total.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 enriched UCR course rows, with course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, prerequisites and planned terms. HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies acquisition, processing and neurocognitive language factors; MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning considers linguistic choices in texts; MCCCOMM111/213/311 study rhetoric and persuasion; MCCCOMM112 teaches basic Dutch; HCBCOGN311 includes language among other higher cognitive functions. DISGATE101 covers Python, DISDATA311 discusses language models within neural networks, BENGATE102 and HCBPSYC211 offer research/statistics, and GOSSOCI212 provides qualitative methods. These are discrete neighbouring perspectives. The workbook has no stand-alone phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, corpus linguistics, sociolinguistics, language-disorder or experimental linguistics progression. It therefore cannot underpin a credible 24-course Linguistics alternative despite useful cognitive, communication and computational components.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: VU's current official pages (checked 2026-09-27) confirm a 180-EC, three-year Bachelor Theologie en Religiewetenschappen offered voltijd and deeltijd, with three co-equal afstudeerrichtingen selected from year 1 (Theologie, Islam, and the selected Religie en Levensbeschouwing/Zingeving route); the deeltijd variant carries the identical 180-EC curriculum at a reduced pace rather than a distinct credit structure. The selected route's own page names its year-by-year course themes -- the origin of religious traditions, world religions and conflict/peacebuilding in year 1; meaning-making/mental health and religion and trauma in year 2; a flexible-location minor plus a scriptieseminar-and-bachelorscriptie and electives such as philosophy of religion in year 3 -- but supplies no EC, compulsory-status or credit-table information for any of them. Resolve the applicable current OER/study-guide credit structure for this exact merged three-route programme, or obtain a current standalone OER document that supersedes the 2017-2018 minor-based structure, before revisiting this comparator.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The normalized target (cp-000119, registry row 127, canonical_name 'B Theology and Religious Studies (deeltijd, Nederlands)', source_provider_id 111A136, programme_unit_code 1001O5760, recognized_programme_code 50910, languages_json=["NLD"], modes_json=["DEELTIJD"]) names no specific route. VU's current official overview page (s0, checked 2026-09-27) confirms a 180-EC, three-year bachelor offered '3 jaar Voltijd en deeltijd' with three co-equal afstudeerrichtingen chosen from year 1: Christelijke theologie (Theologie), Islamitische theologie (Islam, which s0 itself describes as 'the only Islamic-theological WO bachelor in the Netherlands'), and Religie en Levensbeschouwing (also branded 'Zingeving, geestelijke verzorging en samenleving'); s4, a third-party study-choice aggregator republishing VU's own submitted programme data, independently confirms the 180-ECTS total and the same three afstudeerrichtingen. Applying the Section 2.1 neutral route-selection hierarchy (the target is generic and no route is clearly more representative): the Theologie track's own current page (s2) requires a compulsory Hebrew (Hebreeuws I-III) and Greek (Greek I-III + New Testament) biblical-language sequence and offers tradition-specific confessional seminary sub-tracks (Hersteld Hervormd, Baptist, Mennonite); the Islam track requires compulsory Arabic-language study and Qur'an/hadith/fiqh confessional training (s0; independently corroborated by generator-eligible programme-interest rows 5410, 5411, 5412, 5413 naming Qur'an/hadith exegesis, Sharia jurisprudence and Arabic-language study as structural Islam-track content). Religie en Levensbeschouwing is instead described by its own current page (s1) as an explicitly comparative, multireligious, 'dialogisch' course of study engaging several religious traditions rather than forming students within one confessional tradition, with no compulsory classical/liturgical-language sequence. It is therefore the least specialized/most general of the three formal routes and is selected as the reconstructed route. However, s0, s1 and s2 give only qualitative year-by-year course-name lists for their respective tracks (for the selected route: year 1 covers the origin of religious traditions and world religions plus 'Conflict and Peacebuilding'; year 2 covers 'Zingeving, religie en mentale gezondheid' and 'Religie en trauma'; year 3 includes a flexible-location minor, 'Scriptieseminar en bachelorscriptie', and electives such as 'Godsdienstfilosofie') without any EC weight, compulsory-versus-elective status, or credit table for a single component. VU's own current regulations page (s3, checked 2026-09-27) states that the formal Teaching and Examination Regulations for every VU programme are 'published in the Study Guide' at studiegids.vu.nl; that portal's landing page carries only top-level dynamic category navigation with no extractable curriculum content, and a constructed direct URL for this exact study guide entry returned HTTP 404 to available retrieval tools, matching the same dynamic-portal limitation already documented for another current VU counselor target (cp-000118). Reasonable further search located only one standalone official OER PDF for a VU theology bachelor, 'Onderwijs- en Examenregeling Bacheloropleiding Theologie 2017-2018' (s5); its own text shows 'Minor Islam' offered only as one elective minor within a single undifferentiated Theologie bachelor, not as one of three co-equal afstudeerrichtingen chosen from year 1, so it predates and does not reliably describe the current three-route structure and is preserved only as evidence of how substantially the formal structure has since changed, not used to supply component credits. No third-party source (s4; the Qompas study-choice listing checked during research) publishes a per-course EC table either. Because no accessible current or formally adopted source establishes exact EC weights, compulsory/elective status or a stable component list for the selected route, no 180-EC component list is supplied.

The regulations therefore contain no first-year or second-year curriculum outline for the current year and no intake route. The first- and second-year courses are named in the transitional table (Introduction to Fiscal Economics, Quantitative Methods I-III, Microeconomics, Accounting and Financial Reporting, Macroeconomics, Finance, Privaatrecht I, Economy Game, Public Finance, Accounting for Managerial Decision Making, Financial Markets, Ethics Organisations and Society, Belastingrecht voor Particulieren I and II, Belastingrecht voor Ondernemingen I and II) but their EC weights and placement are not established by the reachable current sources, so they are not encoded and no 180-EC pathway is reconstructed.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The defining curriculum of the selected route is a chemical-engineering sequence built on physics and chemistry: Fundamentals of Engineering, Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, and Thermodynamics and Engineering Physics in the compulsory first year, physics, electronics, chemistry and biology laboratory skills, fluid mechanics and heat and mass transfer in year 2, and in year 3 chemical engineering thermodynamics and kinetics, separation processes, reactor engineering, chemical plant design, process design and control, unit-operations and industrial-process-design skills and a 25-EC engineering thesis. UCR offers circular-economy, life-cycle, energy and environmental-engineering-adjacent courses, a mathematics and numerical-methods line and biochemistry and cell-biology courses, but no physics, chemistry sequence, thermodynamics, transport phenomena, reactor or process engineering, mechanics or engineering design. A 24-course programme would be a sustainability-and-mathematics programme with a small circular-economy core padded with unrelated life-science or computing courses, and it would not reproduce the programme's engineering substance; the unmatched components include essentially all of the 25-EC concentration course sequence, the engineering physics and chemistry core and the thesis. The comparison would have to present adjacent sustainability courses as substitutes for engineering content that UCR does not teach.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The 2026-2027 regulations define a 180-EC curriculum of 60 EC per year: year 1 has eight compulsory 5-EC courses, 10 EC of compulsory skills and two 5-EC projects; year 2 has eight elective 5-EC courses and four 2.5-EC elective skills courses chosen from a published framework plus two 5-EC projects; year 3 has one 5-EC core course, a concentration of five 5-EC courses and two 2.5-EC skills courses, and the 25-EC thesis. Of the four concentrations the neutral order rule selects Circular Chemical Engineering. The year-2 electives are an instantiated valid selection of restricted choice; no open free-choice space beyond that framework is published and none is fabricated.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: 2026-2027 (Education and Examination Regulations BSc Circular Engineering, Faculty of Science and Engineering, in force 1 September 2026; programme pages checked 2026-10-03)
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The programme pages (s1, s2) describe the structure in words only: a common first year, a second year of electives, skills and projects, and a third year with one of four concentrations and a thesis; they give no course list with EC. The 180-EC reconstruction therefore uses the 2026-2027 Education and Examination Regulations (s0): Article 3.6 (study load per year), 3.7 (core), 3.8 (electives), 3.9 (concentration and thesis) and Appendix I (course overview). Year 1: eight mandatory 5-EC courses, 10 EC of skills courses and two 5-EC projects. Year 2: eight elective 5-EC courses and four elective 2.5-EC skills courses (two courses and one skill per period, chosen from the published framework) plus two mandatory 5-EC projects; the framework is availability-dependent, so one coherent valid selection linked to the Circular Chemical Engineering concentration is instantiated (Organic Chemistry, Fluid Mechanics, Numerical Methods, Polymeric Materials, Differential Equations, Biochemistry, Heat & Mass Transfer, Remake Reuse Repair Recycle; skills in organic chemistry, statistics, fabrication and design, and analytical and physical chemistry) and is flagged here as an instantiation of restricted choice rather than a fixed requirement. The Heat & Mass Transfer elective is explicitly linked to this concentration, which satisfies the requirement that one elective be linked to a third-year concentration. Year 3: one mandatory 5-EC core course (Ethical and Philosophical Reflections), the Circular Chemical Engineering concentration of five 5-EC courses (the fifth, Circular Process Design and Control, shown in the period 3-4 slot) and two 2.5-EC skills courses, and the 25-EC bachelor thesis (BTH3010). Totals are 60 EC per year and 180 EC overall.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 course rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, prerequisites and planned terms. Relevant adjacent offerings are ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy (life-cycle assessment and circularity), ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation (circular-economy strategies with laboratory skills and inorganic chemistry), ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design (energy systems and technical-economic assessment), ENSDELT111 Building with Nature, DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus (multivariable calculus and differential equations), DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems, DISDATA312 Robotics, HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory. They give partial counterparts to Engineering in a Circular Economy, the Life Cycle Assessment Project, Calculus, Linear Algebra, Multivariate Calculus, Numerical Methods, Differential Equations, Biochemistry and Biotechnology, but none to Fundamentals of Engineering, Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Thermodynamics and Engineering Physics, the physics, electronics and chemistry laboratory skills, Fluid Mechanics, Heat & Mass Transfer, the five-course Circular Chemical Engineering concentration with its skills courses, the design projects or the thesis. No course in the workbook covers physics, thermodynamics, chemical or process engineering, reactor or separation technology, or mechanics, so these isolated adjacent offerings cannot support a coherent 24-course Circular Engineering programme.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current official 2026-2027 OER, established on 9 July 2026 and effective from 1 September 2026, defines a three-year, 180-EC Dutch bachelor in Utrecht. Year 1 is a fixed 60-EC theological foundation. Year 2 combines one 24-EC disciplinary track, Greek (15 EC), Hebrew (15 EC) and 6 EC of personal development and worldview; the OER also permits a no-language replacement pathway, but that is an alternative rather than the primary formal table used here. Year 3 consists of a 30-EC minor, 9 EC in exegesis and source languages, a 6-EC theology/media/current-affairs component and a 15-EC final project. The generic registry target names no track. All four tracks carry the same formal weight, so Systematische Theologie, the first track in the OER's official list, is selected by a neutral source-order tie-break fixed independently of UCR fit. The current target and official sources specify the Utrecht programme; registry interest evidence still points to an older Groningen partnership page, so those stale Groningen-specific interests do not override the authoritative Utrecht curriculum.

None is a dedicated course in Protestant or systematic theology, biblical Greek or Hebrew, scriptural exegesis, historical or practical theology, pastoral formation, Reformation theology or theological research. cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The Groningen programme devotes 120 EC in its first two years to archaeology and then adds archaeological theory, data analysis, research design and a 10-EC archaeology thesis. Required study spans Greek and Roman, north-west European and Arctic archaeology; material culture, conservation and archaeometry; GIS and geoarchaeology; archaeobotany, zooarchaeology and human osteoarchaeology; and two credited fieldwork sequences. UCR has a small but valuable archaeology and heritage group—Introduction to World Archaeology, Greek Archaeology, and Heritage & Ancient Democracy—but no supervised excavation sequence, archaeological-materials or conservation laboratory sequence, bioarchaeology sequence, GIS/geoarchaeology sequence or archaeology thesis. Filling 24 places mainly with history, art, environmental science and generic methods would present neighbouring disciplines as an Archaeology bachelor. No defensible closest 24-course UCR programme can therefore be formed.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The Groningen programme is defined by cumulative proficiency in a chosen European language and by language-specific study through that language. The neutral pathway contains 30 EC of staged German proficiency, 15 EC of German language-specific work across language and society, culture and literature, and politics and society, a further 10-EC interdisciplinary German module, and a thesis grounded in the selected language and profile. UCR's current catalogue contains no German course and no sustained sequence in any European language comparable to this requirement. Its single introductory Dutch course does not create a major-language pathway. UCR literature, media, history, politics, sociology and communication courses can support comparative European questions, but they cannot supply the language competence on which the defining profile and language-specific modules depend. A 24-course response would therefore be a broad European humanities and social-science programme without the programme's central language curriculum, not a defensible closest match.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The normalized target is the generic 180-EC European Languages and Cultures bachelor. The current official curriculum requires one major language and specialization in one or two of three profiles from Year 2. No profile or major language is substantively more representative of the generic degree. The European Language and Society profile and German major are therefore instantiated through the official-order tie-break: Language and Society is listed first among the profiles, and German is listed first among the major-language options. The pathway preserves the formal 60-EC structure of each year, the 10-EC restricted elective, the 30-EC minor, the 10-EC thesis and every language-specific component without inventing optional content.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows with course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. MCCCOMM112 Dutch is the only course whose primary purpose is proficiency in a European language; it is one introductory 7.5-EC course and does not continue into intermediate or advanced study. UCR offers no German course and no sequence in French, Italian, Russian, Spanish or Swedish. MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning and HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics support general linguistic analysis; MCCLITR courses support literature; MCCMEDI courses support media and cultural analysis; and GOSHIST, GOSPOLI, GOSSOCI and GOSLAWJ courses support European historical, political and social study. These courses could form coherent European Studies or communication programmes, but they cannot reproduce cumulative major-language proficiency, language-specific profile study and a thesis grounded in that language. Because the missing language sequence is the degree's academic foundation rather than a peripheral specialty, 23 non-PPD UCR courses cannot form a defensible European Languages and Cultures programme.

cases.programme_display_name: Bachelor Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences
cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: TU/e's AUBS bachelor is a project- and studio-intensive built-environment engineering degree. Its common first year integrates calculus, architecture and the city, urban systems, healthy and sustainable environments, structural statics, circularity and energy performance, and structure and architecture with four successive design or research projects. The later programme requires one of four coherent tracks and its project sequence: architectural and urban design, building physics and services, structural engineering and design, or urban systems and real estate. All routes culminate in multidisciplinary project work and a discipline-specific Bachelor End Project. UCR offers useful adjacent courses in spatial planning, GIS and earth observation, sustainable energy and life-cycle analysis, nature-based design, product design, heritage and quantitative methods. It has no architecture or urban-design studio sequence, building-physics and building-services sequence, structural statics and materials progression, construction-technology education, architectural drawing and modelmaking formation, or built-environment engineering capstone. A 24-course UCR programme would therefore replace the target's defining studio, technical and project spine with adjacent liberal-arts and sustainability study and would not be an academically defensible comparison.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The official 2026-2027 AUBS guide and current Education Guide account for all 180 EC as 130 EC core, 40 EC electives and 10 EC ITEC. Year one is common and explicitly orients students across AUDE, BPS, SED and USRE through built-environment courses and four projects. In years two and three, students choose one track, complete its core courses and projects, and use genuine elective space for depth, cross-track study or a thematic profile. The current guide requires a multidisciplinary project before the 10-EC Bachelor End Project. Illustrative named course and project lists include Histories of Architecture and Urbanism, Architecture and Technology, Dimensioning of Structures, Urban Planning, Building Services, Concrete and Masonry Structures, Steel and Timber Structures and Applied Mechanics, Building Performance, Urban Physics, Sustainable Retrofit, Regenerative Building Design, structural and architectural design projects, urban-mobility projects and the final disciplinary project. The aggregate 130-EC core component preserves the complete degree without pretending that four mutually exclusive tracks are simultaneously compulsory.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: TU/e's current official programme, Education Guide and 2026-2027 Bachelor AUBS Course Guide, checked 2026-10-03, describe a three-year, 180-EC bachelor for students starting in 2023-2024 and after. The common first year combines calculus and built-environment theory with four successive projects and orientation across Architectural Urban Design and Engineering, Building Physics and Services, Structural Engineering and Design, and Urban Systems and Real Estate. Students then select one track, take its core courses and projects, complete a multidisciplinary project and finish with a 10-EC Bachelor End Project. The complete 130/40/10 allocation is retained below because the official guide defines the variable track and elective curriculum rather than one universal course list.

Students learn through core and elective courses, multidisciplinary projects, coaching, reflection and portfolio development, progressively combining user observation and testing, interaction and behavioural design, programming and data, physical computing and sensors, rapid prototyping and digital fabrication, product aesthetics, systems thinking, sustainability, business propositions and responsible innovation. The Bachelor Final Project requires those competencies to be integrated in an independently shaped intelligent or interactive product, system or service rather than treated as unrelated electives.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: Leiden's adopted 2026-2027 Archaeology regulations state that the programme no longer has specialisations for new entrants; World Archaeology and Heritage and Society remain applicable only to students who started in or before 2025-2026. The same regulations establish a 180-EC degree with 150 EC of compulsory components and up to 30 EC of optional study. The missing applicable third-year structure cannot be inferred from the outgoing curriculum without inventing compulsory, elective, research and thesis requirements.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The applicable revised curriculum is supported for 120 EC: 60 EC in Year 1 and 60 EC in Year 2, each composed of twelve compulsory 5-EC modules. It establishes integrated criminological theory, legal and criminal-justice study, psychological and sociological explanations, qualitative and quantitative methods, professional skills, policy evaluation, victims and offenders, cybercrime, investigation and prosecution, forensic psychology and experimental methods. The current product confirms that the programme as a whole is 180 EC, but the remaining revised 60 EC are not yet published. The legacy Year 3 shown in the same product is deliberately excluded because Leiden restricts it to earlier cohorts.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The live Leiden Study Guide product confirms a current 180-EC Criminology bachelor and supplies the revised first and second years in full. Each contains twelve compulsory 5-EC modules, together establishing 120 EC in criminology, law, criminal justice, psychology, sociology, qualitative and quantitative research, policy evaluation, victims, offenders, cybercrime, investigation, prosecution and experiments. The same product explicitly states that its displayed third year is the old curriculum for students who began in 2024 or earlier and that Year 3 of the revised curriculum will first be included in the 2027-2028 Study Guide. Because a Fall 2026 entrant cannot combine the revised Years 1-2 with that legacy Year 3, only the supported 120 EC of the applicable revised curriculum are retained. The zero-credit Language Test Criminology, Tutoring/LLP Criminology and Leiden Law Practices entries are noted in the official product but omitted from the positive-credit component list.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The supported non-duplicated curriculum totals 175 EC. It establishes a 60-EC revised first year in German language, linguistics, literature, culture and digital humanities; 55 EC of identifiable second-year progression including advanced German, language history, cultural memory, philosophy of science and a compulsory 25-EC stay at a German-speaking university; and a 60-EC third-year structure of 20 EC restricted-choice specialisation, a 10-EC German-studies thesis and 30 EC open elective space. provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The live 2026-2027 product confirms a 180-EC bachelor organised through German-language proficiency, German linguistics, German literature and cultural studies, a compulsory 25-EC stay at a German-speaking university, third-year specialisation, 30 EC of open elective space and a 10-EC bachelor thesis. Its current Year 1 totals 60 EC. The same product lists the identical 5-EC course Kämpfen, beten, schreiben: Literatur von 750 bis 1700 under both Years 1 and 2. Counting it twice would create an impossible same-course duplication; counting it once leaves the published first two years at 115 EC. The archived 2025-2026 guide shows the outgoing cohort structure: its first year used Deutschland in Bildern and Die Erfindung der deutschen Kultur, while Die Erfindung der deutschen Kultur also completed that cohort's second year. This confirms that the live Year 2 block is cohort-transitional rather than a coherent continuation of the revised Fall 2026 first year. The supported non-duplicated components total 175 EC and are retained; the missing 5-EC component is not invented.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden Tax Law is a cumulative Dutch legal degree with a specialist fiscal spine. Its compulsory curriculum combines the foundations of constitutional, private, criminal, international, European, administrative, Roman, obligations and company law with income taxation, value added and real-estate transfer taxation, corporation tax, international tax law, procedural and formal tax law, financial accounting, public-sector economics, tax ethics, fiscal advocacy and a Tax Law thesis. UCR offers a useful six-course law-and-justice sequence plus economics, public economics, accounting and business-law courses, but no dedicated tax-law course or progression in income, corporate, indirect, international, procedural and formal taxation. A 24-course UCR pathway could examine law, markets and public policy broadly, but it could not preserve the target's academic identity as Tax Law.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The live Leiden Study Guide identifies a three-year, 180-EC Tax Law bachelor. The first year establishes a broad Dutch-law foundation and introduces tax law and legal methods. The second year combines private, criminal, European and company law with individual income taxation, value added and real-estate transfer taxation, financial accounting, public-sector economics and the ethics of taxation. The third year requires tax-law moot court, procedural and formal tax law, public-sector economics, tax ethics, international tax law, corporation tax and a bachelor thesis, while preserving 15 EC of genuine elective space. No formal route or specialisation is required for the generic normalized target; the programme's full-time curriculum supplies the academically neutral content reconstruction for the registered full-time and part-time modes.

GOSGATE102 Law, Society & Justice, GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, GOSLAWJ211 Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, GOSLAWJ212 Introduction to Public International Law, GOSLAWJ213 Comparative Constitutional Law, GOSLAWJ311 Principles of Private Law and GOSLAWJ312 Foundations of European Union Law provide meaningful broad legal formation. BENECON111 Introduction to Economics, BENECON211 International Macroeconomics, BENECON212 Microeconomics & Behavior, BENECON311 Public Economics and BENECON312 Econometrics provide economic and policy analysis; BENBUSI112 Accounting & Corporate Finance and BENBUSI311 Transnational Business Law add adjacent accounting and business-law study. Public Economics explicitly addresses taxation, public goods, externalities and government spending, but the workbook contains no dedicated tax law, individual income taxation, corporation tax, value added or transfer tax, international taxation, fiscal procedure, formal tax law, taxpayer-rights or tax-enforcement course, no Dutch administrative and obligations-law progression, and no fiscal moot court or Tax Law thesis. The closest possible UCR combination would consequently be an interdisciplinary law-and-economics pathway, not a defensible substitute for the comparator's specialist fiscal-law sequence.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden French Language and Culture is a cumulative French-medium language-and-humanities degree. Its defining compulsory formation integrates sustained advanced French speaking, listening and academic writing through C1 with grammar, syntax, phonology, French linguistics, literature across historical periods, French and Francophone cultural history, programme-specific research seminars and a French-focused thesis. UCR offers strong English-medium courses in literary, communication, film, media, historical and cultural analysis plus one psycholinguistics course, but it has no taught French-language acquisition sequence and no French or Francophone studies curriculum. A 24-course UCR pathway could study literature, media, identity and postcolonial questions comparatively, but it could not preserve the target's academic identity as French Language and Culture.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The official curriculum accounts for the full 180 EC as 60 EC of fixed first-year French language, linguistics, literature and culture study; 80 EC of upper-year programme-specific language and humanities formation; 30 EC of genuine free-choice space; and a 10-EC BA thesis. The current cohort rules require multiple French-programme seminars, including research seminars, alongside advanced written and oral language work. Leiden's official programme material states that classes are French-medium and foregrounds the Francophone world beyond France. Even after the 30-EC free-choice block is preserved, the remaining 150 EC form a connected French-proficiency and French/Francophone-studies core rather than a collection of general humanities electives.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: Latest target-specific official curriculum (2025-2026), checked against the live 2026-2027 catalogue on 2026-10-07
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: Leiden's latest published target-specific study guide identifies a three-year, 180-EC French Language and Culture bachelor centred on French proficiency, linguistics, literature and cultural study. The fully fixed 60-EC first year combines advanced French, oral comprehension and expression, grammar, phonology, French linguistics, literary studies across periods and French cultural history. The upper years continue written and oral French to C1, syntax, Francophone literatures and societies, modern literature, poetry and theatre, research methodology, programme seminars and a 10-EC thesis, while preserving 30 EC of genuine free-choice space. The official programme brochure confirms that teaching is conducted in French and that the programme develops specialist knowledge of French language, literature and culture in France and the wider Francophone world. No formal route or specialisation is required for the generic normalized target; alternating seminars are represented as programme seminar space rather than filled with an invented choice.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature, MCCLITR212 Life & Travel Writing, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide substantial comparative literary study. MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning adds linguistic and close-reading methods; HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies language acquisition, use and comprehension; and the communication, film, media, history, sociology and heritage offerings support analysis of culture, identity, colonialism, decolonial critique and representation. The workbook nevertheless contains no French-language course at any level, no staged speaking, listening, grammar, phonetics or academic-writing sequence in French, no French linguistics, no historical sequence in French literature, no dedicated French or Francophone cultural-studies course, no French-medium research seminar and no French-focused thesis. Psycholinguistics is a general cognitive-science course rather than language instruction, and the literature and media courses are comparative English-medium offerings rather than a French/Francophone disciplinary spine. No academically honest 24-course closest match can therefore supply the target programme's cumulative language proficiency and area-specific formation.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden Medicine is an integrated medical-professional bachelor whose defining formation combines cellular and organ-system science with disease mechanisms, clinically oriented patient problems, pharmacology, longitudinal medical progress testing, patient communication, professional behaviour, care-stage and early-practice contact, clinical reasoning, history taking and physical examination. UCR offers a strong biomedical, behavioural and public-health curriculum, but no supervised patient-care placement, clinical examination and history-taking sequence, integrated diagnostic-reasoning progression, longitudinal medical-professional assessment or comprehensive clinically organized organ-system curriculum. A 24-course UCR programme could provide excellent preparation in biomedical and health sciences, but it would not be a defensible Medicine comparator.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The latest complete official programme table accounts for exactly 180 EC: 60 EC per year. Year 1 integrates normal cellular, molecular and organ-system structure and function with a care internship, academic/scientific training, communication and professional skills, ethics, law, prevention, health promotion, technology and the medical progress test. Year 2 advances through disease mechanisms, pharmacology and integrated clinical-problem blocks supported by longitudinal academic and professional formation. Year 3 preserves 15 EC of genuine faculty elective space and combines reproduction, mental health and hormones, ageing and emergency-care problem blocks with clinical skills, early practice contacts, academic critical appraisal and the progress test. The bachelor endpoint is distributed across assessed clinical and research outputs rather than isolated as one separately credited thesis.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: Current programme checked 2026-10-07; latest complete official curriculum table 2025-2026
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current Leiden and LUMC programme pages confirm the three-year Medicine bachelor and its continuing structure: first-year cellular, molecular, organ-system, academic and professional foundations with patient contact; second-year disease mechanisms and clinically integrated problem blocks; and third-year faculty choice space, clinically oriented problem blocks, clinical skills and longitudinal academic and professional formation. The latest complete target-specific official table accounts for 60 EC in each year. Year 3 begins with 15 EC of genuine faculty elective space, preserved without inventing a choice. The bachelor endpoint is assessed through the CAT project, internal-medicine and neurological examinations, and the selected half-minor report rather than a separately credited thesis course. The programme has no formal route or specialisation requiring selection.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide substantial biomedical foundations. HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease add advanced biomedical content; HCBGATE102 Introduction to Brain & Behavior and the cognition and psychology sequences cover neural, behavioural and mental-health perspectives; HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBPSYC311 Medical & Health Psychology and quantitative research courses add population, behavioural and evidence perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no supervised clinical placement or patient-care course, no patient interviewing and physical-examination sequence, no longitudinal clinical-skills assessment, no integrated diagnostic-reasoning curriculum, no medicine-wide progress testing, and no comprehensive clinical-problem progression across organ systems and life stages. The available biomedical courses therefore support a biomedical-science alternative, not the profession-defining academic and clinical formation of Medicine.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden Classics is defined by cumulative ancient Greek and Latin language acquisition, sustained reading of prose and poetry in both original languages, philological and linguistic analysis, and advanced independent reading and research across the two languages. UCR offers valuable study of ancient history, archaeology, philosophy, literature, myth, art and reception, but no Greek or Latin language-acquisition sequence and no curriculum of primary classical texts in the original languages. Those are not peripheral specialist additions: they organize the Leiden programme from the first year through the thesis. A UCR ancient-world pathway would therefore be a defensible Ancient Studies programme, but not a defensible comparator for this language-and-philology-centred Classics degree.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The latest complete official programme table accounts for exactly 180 EC: 60 EC per year. Year 1 contains 20 EC of Greek and Latin language acquisition and 20 EC of original-language prose, rhetoric, drama and lyric/elegy, integrated with ancient history, philosophy, literary theory and literary history. Year 2 continues Greek and Latin texts, epic, drama, Greek linguistics and Renaissance Latin while adding material culture, source transmission, philosophy of science and a restricted ancient-philosophy choice. Year 3 preserves 30 EC of genuine free choice and requires 15 EC of advanced Greek/Latin reading, late-antique philosophy and religion, and a 10-EC thesis; both classical languages must remain represented.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current official programme page confirms Classics as an integrated study of ancient Greek and Latin language and literature, ancient history, philosophy, archaeology and the later reception of antiquity. The latest complete target-specific official study guide supplies a coherent 180-EC structure: 60 EC in each year. Year 1 combines four 5-EC Greek and Latin acquisition modules with four original-language literature courses and history, philosophy, literary theory and literary history. Year 2 continues original-language prose, drama, epic, linguistics and Renaissance Latin alongside material culture, source transmission, philosophy of science and a restricted thematic choice. Year 3 preserves 30 EC of genuine free-choice space and requires a Greek or Latin workshop, an independent reading list in the other language, late-antique philosophy and religion, and a 10-EC thesis. No formal route or specialization is selected.

MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology, MCCHEAM213 Greek Archaeology, MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy, GOSHIST213 Western Way of War, GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy, MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature provide substantial ancient-world, philosophical, literary and material-culture perspectives; MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean and MCCCOMM111 The Art of Rhetorical Communication support reception and rhetoric. The workbook nevertheless contains no ancient Greek course, no Latin course, no cumulative grammar and vocabulary sequence, no sustained original-language reading of Greek and Roman prose and poetry, no classical philology or Greek linguistics sequence, and no advanced Greek/Latin independent reading. Because those missing elements constitute the degree's continuous disciplinary spine, the available ancient-history, archaeology and literature courses support Ancient Studies rather than a defensible Classics match.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden International Studies is not merely a broad collection of global politics, economics, history and culture courses. Every student selects one world region, studies that region through all four disciplinary perspectives, completes a cumulative 25-EC associated-language sequence plus a 5-EC language-and-culture-in-practice course, and writes an area-specific thesis. UCR offers strong adjacent work in international relations, economics, history, law, sociology, media and sustainability, but its current curriculum contains only one general Dutch course and no sustained regional-language sequence. It also lacks a coherent four-perspective area curriculum for any one of the eight Leiden regions. Filling 24 UCR slots with globally oriented courses would therefore reproduce breadth while discarding the degree's defining language-plus-regional-specialisation architecture.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The latest complete official study-guide table accounts for exactly 180 EC: 60 EC per year. Year 1 establishes academic literacy, cultural studies, economics, politics, sociolinguistics and world history, then begins a selected region through culture/language, history and 10 EC of language acquisition. Year 2 adds the region's economy and politics, cross-cultural communication, research methods, global political economy, international relations, philosophy of science, a thematic seminar and 15 further EC in the same language. Year 3 contains 30 EC of genuine elective space and requires a 10-EC consultancy project, 5 EC of language and culture in practice, and a 15-EC area-specific thesis. Africa with Arabic is instantiated only by the official-order tie-break; the same structural mismatch applies to all eight areas and their linked languages.

MCCHEAM211 African Art & Heritage and MCCMEDI311 Media & Race provide valuable regionally relevant cultural perspectives, while BENENTR312 International Business & Governance and the communication curriculum support international professional applications. cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden Italian Language and Culture is organized around cumulative Italian proficiency and sustained Italian-language study of linguistics, literature, culture and society. Its compulsory sequence progresses from Lingua italiana Ia/Ib/Ic through IIa/IIb, while subject courses cover Italian phonology, morphology, syntax, language history and variation, medieval through contemporary literature, and Italian cultural history. The thesis may be written in Italian. UCR offers strong adjacent humanities courses, including one focused on Renaissance Italy, but no Italian language instruction, no Italian-language source-analysis sequence and no Italian linguistics. A 24-course UCR pathway in general European history, literature, film, communication and art would therefore replace the degree's continuous language-and-area core rather than provide a defensible comparator.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The latest complete official programme accounts for exactly 180 EC: fixed 60-EC first and second years, followed by 20 EC of Italian subject work, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 10-EC BA thesis in Year 3. Year 1 contains 20 EC of Italian proficiency alongside Italian literature, culture, linguistics and Romance linguistics. Year 2 contains 20 further EC of Italian proficiency plus Italian poetry, contemporary language, present-day Italy, Dante, modern literature, history of Italian and a subject research paper. Year 3 continues Italian literature and linguistics through fixed and monographic courses before the thesis. The official programme outcomes target high Italian proficiency, analysis of Italian phonology, morphology, syntax and semantics, recognition of historical, geographical and sociolinguistic variants, and knowledge of Italian literary and cultural history.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: Current programme checked 2026-10-07; latest complete official curriculum table and programme-specific regulations 2025-2026
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current official programme page confirms a language-centred Italian Studies degree: students develop spoken and written Italian, study Italian linguistics, literature, culture and society, and are prepared to write the thesis in Italian. The latest complete official study guide supplies a coherent 180-EC structure: fixed 60-EC first and second years, followed by 20 EC of Italian subject work, 30 EC of genuine elective space and a 10-EC thesis in Year 3. The first two listed monographic options are instantiated neutrally; the open elective space is not populated with invented subjects.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean directly addresses Renaissance Italian art and Mediterranean connections, while MCCHEAM111 Introduction to Western Art History supplies broader European art-historical context. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide literary methods; MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media supports film analysis; GOSHIST111 Modern History provides European historical context. MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning examines linguistic choices in texts and HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies language processing, but neither teaches Italian. The workbook contains no Italian course, no cumulative Italian grammar, vocabulary, listening, speaking, reading or writing sequence, no study of Italian phonology, morphology, syntax, dialects or minority languages, no sustained Italian-language literary curriculum, and no Italian-language thesis preparation. The adjacent Renaissance, history, literature, film and language-science courses cannot substitute for the compulsory Italian-language disciplinary spine.

prerequisites:
Voor toegang tot dit vak zijn geen specifieke vaardigheden vereist.

Studenten van de bachelors Franse taal en cultuur en Italiaanse taal en cultuur, de minor Middeleeuwen en vroegmoderne tijd, de minor Frans en de Franstalige wereld en de pre-masters Literary Studies en Linguistics hebben voorrang bij het volgen van dit vak. Andere studenten kunnen het vak volgen in het geval er plek is.

NB: dit vak bestaat uit wekelijkse hoorcolleges een aanvullende werkcolleges. Van alle studenten wordt verwacht dat ze aanwezig zijn bij de hoorcolleges. De werkcolleges, die in het derde uur van de colleges worden gegeven, spitsen zich afwisselend toe op Franse en Italiaanse literatuur. Het exacte schema wordt via Brightspace bekendgemaakt. Hierbij geldt:
\- studenten Frans zijn aanwezig bij de werkcolleges Frans \(die in de doeltaal gegeven worden\)\.
\- studenten Italiaans zijn aanwezig bij de werkcolleges Italiaans \(in het Nederlands\)\.
\- minor\- en keuzevakstudenten kiezen zelf voor werkcolleges in één van deze twee talen\. Deze keuze is tevens bepalend voor de toetsing\. Studenten van de minor Frans en de Franstalige Wereld volgen de werkcolleges Frans\.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden’s 180-EC Japanese Studies pathway joins a compulsory, progressive Japanese-language sequence with Japanese history, society, material culture, literary/media seminars, Japanese-source research and a thesis. The selected pathway includes 55 EC of dedicated Modern Japanese language courses, with further selected classical-language and Japan-focused practice components before its research component, and several additional Japan-specific courses. UCR offers no Japanese-language course and no course whose current content addresses Japan specifically. Its general history, politics, art, literature and media courses could support a comparative or global-culture programme, but would not implement a Japan-focused 24-course academic concept or reproduce its language-based source work. A purported closest UCR Japanese Studies alternative would depend on generic disciplinary neighbours and misrepresent the core.
cases.audit_scope: External-programme identity, defining curriculum, credit/choice reconstruction and source context; no independent UCR feasibility assessment
cases.audit_basis: The stored Japanese course weights and selected Leiden/thesis pathway still close 60 + 60 + 60. However, required first-year society, arts, modern history and regional courses explicitly use English, while normalized metadata say only NLD. No formal graduation specialisation is applicable.
cases.recommended_fix: Retain the verified Japanese 180-EC structure, the lawful Leiden alternative, HUM choices and thesis/seminar endpoint. Correct NLD + ENG instruction metadata; Dutch remains the formal programme classification, Japanese language learning is not automatically Japanese-medium teaching, and required English courses must be stated explicitly.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The official 2026–27 study BA-JAP identifies 60 EC of first-year compulsory units, a 20-EC second-year compulsory group with 40 EC of restricted choices, and a 60-EC third year comprising 15 EC of restricted specialist study, one 15-EC graduation project pathway and 30 EC of actual elective space. The BA Thesis pathway is selected. The OER confirms Japanese-language progression and primary-source competence and describes HUM and SOSCI as clusters for course choices, not formal graduation tracks. The selected external components preserve all 180 EC without counting mutually exclusive Japan stay, alternative seminars or non-curricular language preparation.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: 2026–27 Leiden Study Guide and programme-specific OER, checked 2026-09-26
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current 2026–27 Leiden Study Guide study BA-JAP and its public product API identify 60 EC in each year. The chosen coherent pathway selects the Leiden 15-EC second-year route (Modern Japanese 2c, 10 EC, and a second shared East Asian course, 5 EC), rather than the Japan study-abroad route; one permitted option in each seminar and restricted-choice group; the BA Thesis 10 EC plus Graduation Seminar 5 EC rather than other graduation projects; and the full 30 EC genuine third-year elective space, split into two 15-EC components. The 0-EC mentorship and non-curricular JLPT preparation are excluded. The adopted OER confirms no formal graduation tracks and the 2026–27 language progression. Course EC were checked against the public 2026–27 module entries; the study grouping and selected options account for exactly 180 EC.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics and methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. The workbook contains no Japanese, Korean, Chinese or East Asian course or language sequence. GOSHIST111/211/312 address modern history, empires and historical research without a Japan focus; GOSPOLI112/212/313 cover comparative politics, international relations and conflict without Japan-specific training. MCCHEAM111/212 and MCCLITR111/311 or MCCMEDI111/211 offer art, literature and media methods but no Japanese materials or language. Linguistic study in HCBCOGN312 is psycholinguistics, not Japanese instruction. These courses cannot make 23 non-PPD courses each contribute concretely to a Japan-centred concept, and no timetable can repair that substantive gap.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden’s Korean Studies bachelor integrates a cumulative Korean-language sequence with Korean history, thought, culture, society, politics and region-specific methods. The chosen 180-EC pathway includes 65 EC of dedicated Korean-language and Korean-reading courses before the thesis (Korean 1–3, Korean Language in Use, Intermediate Korean Reading 1 and 2A, and Business Korean), and further Korean-centred seminars and primary-source work. UCR has no Korean-language course and no Korea-specific history, media, literature or politics course. A curriculum of 24 UCR courses drawn from broadly related social sciences and humanities would fail the requirement that each non-PPD course contribute concretely to the target-specific concept. It would conceal the central language and Korea-based source-training gap, so no defensible closest UCR alternative can be constructed.
cases.audit_scope: External-programme identity, defining curriculum, credit/choice reconstruction and source context; no independent UCR feasibility assessment
cases.audit_basis: The stored Korean pathway remains 60 + 60 + 60, including Korean 3 in Leiden at 15, Themes and Approaches at 10, two subject choices and open 30. The choice-group prose says 5 for the Themes/Hanmun slot but its group and current module give 10; the module/group credit controls. Required Korean 1/2 and other current required modules use English, omitted by NLD-only metadata.
cases.recommended_fix: Retain the weighted current pathway and its valid methods, regional, language and topical choices. Correct NLD + ENG instruction metadata and distinguish Korean as the subject language. Retain Business Korean unless thesis eligibility for the earlier-listed Academic Purposes option is established; no formal route is invented.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The 2026–27 official catalogue shows first year 50 EC compulsory plus two 5-EC restricted choices; second year 20 EC compulsory and 40 EC specified restricted choices; third year a 5-EC compulsory thesis seminar, 15 EC of restricted language/topic study, a 10-EC final paper and 30 EC of free elective space. A single coherent option was selected in each restricted group. The programme-specific adopted OER confirms language progression from Korean 1 through Korean 3, further reading and final source-based work. No formal graduation route is named. All 180 EC are accounted for exactly once.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: 2026–27 Leiden Study Guide and programme-specific OER, checked 2026-09-26
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current 2026–27 Leiden Study Guide study BA-KOR and its public product API identify 60 EC in each year. The chosen coherent pathway selects one permitted first-year 5-EC methods course and one 5-EC regional course; Korean 3 (15 EC) rather than the alternative Korea study-language component; Themes and Approaches (10 EC) rather than Hanmun; two of the five 5-EC second-year subject electives; Intermediate Korean Reading 2A; one third-year language course and one 10-EC topical seminar. The 10-EC BA Final paper and 5-EC seminar are compulsory. Thirty EC of genuinely open third-year elective space are preserved as two 15-EC components. The 0-EC mentorship and non-curricular group are excluded. The adopted OER confirms no formal graduation tracks and the Korean-language prerequisites. Current module EC and the selected study groups were checked on 2026-09-26 and sum to 180 EC.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. No UCR course teaches Korean or specifically covers either Korea, Korean cultural sources or Korean history. GOSHIST111/211/312 cover modern history, empires and historical research without the Korean sequence; GOSPOLI112/212/313 address comparative politics, international relations and conflict without Korea-specific material. MCCMEDI111/211, MCCLITR111/311 and MCCHEAM111 can teach media, literature and art methods, but not Korean-language source reading or the Korea-centred historical and cultural curriculum. HCBCOGN312 examines psycholinguistics rather than Korean language acquisition. Those neighbouring methods do not sustain 23 substantively relevant non-PPD courses for a Korean Studies concept; semester feasibility cannot cure the subject mismatch.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: A valid 24-course UCR programme cannot represent this Latin American Studies bachelor’s defining combination of sustained Latin America-specific history, culture, politics, linguistics, Spanish/Portuguese language progression and study abroad. UCR has no Spanish or Portuguese language course or sequence, and only incidental Latin American examples within broader global courses. Filling 24 places with general history, politics, sociology, media or literature would change the target into general global studies and falsely imply regional and language preparation that UCR does not offer.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The 2026–27 Leiden curriculum has a 40-EC Latin American/linguistic first-year core plus 20 EC Spanish language, a second year with 10 EC compulsory core, 20 EC Spanish-speaking route content and a mandatory 30-EC study abroad, and a final year with 15 EC compulsory study, a 5-EC restricted choice, a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC open elective space. Spanish was selected as one internally coherent option; the alternative Brazil/Portuguese option likewise requires sustained region-specific language training. OER Article 2.2 says no formal graduation route, so routeSelection is null despite the study guide’s language-choice groups. The 2026–27 OER introduces a revised first year; later years here are the currently published guide structure and may change for later cohorts.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: Leiden’s current 2026–27 Study Guide product and public API give 60 EC in each year. This coherent curriculum instantiates the Spanish-language option rather than the Brazil/Portuguese option: first-year Spanish 1 and 2 (20 EC), second-year Spanish 3 (10 EC) together with Spanish-speaking regional subjects (10 EC). The choice reflects the programme’s broader Spanish-speaking Latin American scope, not UCR availability. The remaining first-year foundation is 40 EC of linguistics, Latin American history, literatures and images, languages, Indigeneities and humanities core; second year also has 10 EC compulsory core and a required 30-EC study-abroad semester. Third year has 15 EC compulsory Latin American/world and research-methods work, one first-listed 5-EC restricted choice (Public Policies in Latin America), a 10-EC BA thesis and 30 EC genuine open elective space. The 0-EC thesis seminar and non-curricular language electives are omitted from the 180-EC component list. The 2026–27 programme-specific OER says no formal graduation tracks and confirms advanced Spanish/Portuguese competence and the required study-abroad and research progression; it notes that a new first year begins in 2026–27. The record represents the complete published 2026–27 structure, not a guarantee about later curricular revisions for the 2026 entry cohort.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall-2026-cohort availability. The catalogue has Dutch (MCCCOMM112) but no Spanish or Portuguese language course. GOSHIST211 History of Empires, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations, GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict and GOSSOCI214 Modern Sociology cover general comparative or colonial questions, not a sustained Latin American regional curriculum. GOSSOCI311 New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory mentions a Latin American civil-society case, but this is one example in a general global-sociology course. GOSHIST311 Native American Histories focuses on North America, not Latin America. MCCMEDI212 Media & the Environment treats Indigenous and postcolonial media generally. These courses could support selected adjacent questions, but they do not supply three years of Latin American history, culture, politics, language proficiency and the 30-EC abroad component. Their assembly into 24 courses would not be a defensible closest-match programme.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: A valid 24-course UCR programme cannot represent this Physics bachelor’s defining sequence of mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum mechanics, statistical and solid-state physics, repeated experimental laboratories and a 27-EC independent physics research project. The current UCR catalogue contains mathematics, programming and energy/sustainability courses but no physics course sequence or physics laboratory. Filling the remaining places with adjacent mathematics, data science, engineering or sustainability courses would change the target into a different interdisciplinary programme and falsely imply foundational and advanced physics training that UCR does not provide.
