provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The current official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC: 60 EC compulsory first year; 51 EC compulsory second year plus an instantiated 9-EC restricted physics choice; and 30 EC of instantiated physics core-package options, a separate 3-EC physics choice, and a 27-EC bachelor research project in year three. The programme has no named graduation route, so routeSelection is null. Its academic identity is sustained theoretical, mathematical and experimental physics rather than a collection of broadly science-related electives.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The official 2026–27 Leiden study product defines a 180-EC Physics bachelor: a 60-EC compulsory first year, 51 EC of compulsory second-year physics and mathematics plus 9 EC of restricted physics choices, and a third year with a 30-EC elective/core-package space, a separate 3-EC restricted physics choice and a 27-EC bachelor research project. To instantiate one coherent physics-centred pathway, the second-year 9 EC selects Astro-Particle Physics (6 EC) and Fluid Phenomena in Soft Matter (3 EC); the third-year 30-EC core package selects the first five remaining 6-EC physics options in official order, and the separate 3 EC selects Relativistic Electrodynamics. These choices preserve the published rules and are made independently of UCR fit. The university’s public programme pages describe the same theoretical-and-experimental foundation, free-specialisation semester and culminating independent physics research project.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall-2026-cohort availability. UCR offers DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics, as well as DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming. Those courses provide useful mathematical and computational tools, but the catalogue contains no course in classical mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum mechanics, statistical physics, solid-state physics, astrophysics or experimental physics, and no physics laboratory or physics research sequence. ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design concern energy systems and sustainable design rather than foundational physics. cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: A valid 24-course UCR programme cannot represent the defining Dutch-specific language, linguistics, literature, media and historical-text curriculum of Leiden’s Dutch Language and Culture bachelor. UCR offers one introductory Dutch language course but no Dutch-language progression, Dutch linguistics sequence, Dutch literature sequence or sustained study of Dutch cultural texts. A schedule filled with general rhetoric, literature, media and history would change the target into general communication and cultural studies and falsely imply Dutch disciplinary preparation.

The stored Dutch Linguistics package contains the two required 10-EC linguistics units plus three permitted 10-EC cross-specialisation choices; Recent Novels is permissible within this package. The formal OER says no graduation directions apply, so a formal route must remain unspecified.
cases.recommended_fix: Retain the external basis, internal Dutch Linguistics selection, bound 50 and open 30. Preserve the distinction between programme-level Dutch instruction and a selected English-medium Recent Novels option; do not add an unverified universal English language or formal route.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The complete 180-EC comparator contains 60 EC of foundational Dutch language, literature, rhetoric and media study; 30 EC of compulsory second-year disciplinary work; a 50-EC Dutch Linguistics specialisation choice; a 10-EC Dutch-linguistics thesis; and 30 EC open electives. The internal linguistics choice remains embedded in a programme whose common core covers older and modern Dutch literature, the history and social use of Dutch, Dutch media and historical Dutch texts. The OER does not recognize formal graduation directions, hence routeSelection is null.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current 2026–27 Leiden study product accounts for 180 EC: a 60-EC first-year core, 30 EC of second-year compulsory work, 50 EC of internal specialisation study spanning years two and three, a 10-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC open elective space. The Dutch Linguistics specialisation group is instantiated because it most directly preserves the programme’s broad Dutch-language identity; its two 10-EC compulsory courses and the first three eligible 10-EC listed choices make the required 50 EC. This choice is made independently of UCR fit. The 0-EC mentoring and thesis-seminar modules are omitted. The 2026–27 programme-specific OER states that formal graduation directions are not applicable, so routeSelection is null even though the study product organises the 50-EC bound-choice space into internal specialisation groups.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall-2026-cohort availability. MCCCOMM112 Dutch is a single introductory language course focused on uncomplicated everyday communication; it is not an academic Dutch sequence. HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics examines general language processing and cognition, while MCCCOMM111 The Art of Rhetorical Communication, MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning, MCCCOMM311 Persuasive Communication and MCCCOMM213 Rhetoric in Action provide general rhetoric and communication methods. MCCLITR111/112/311/312 offer broad literary analysis, and MCCMEDI111/112/211/311 offer general media study. None provides sustained Dutch linguistics, historical Dutch, Dutch literary history or Dutch-language primary-source work. These courses can support adjacent questions but cannot give 23 non-PPD courses a concrete Dutch Language and Culture rationale or reproduce the comparator’s disciplinary progression.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: A valid 24-course UCR programme cannot represent this professionally structured Notarial Law bachelor. UCR provides a small general law cluster, including private, criminal, constitutional, international, European and human-rights law, but it has no sustained sequence in property and real-estate law, matrimonial property, succession, family law, company structures for civil-law notaries, tax law, civil procedure or notarial drafting and practice. Filling the programme with politics, philosophy or general business courses would not reproduce the target’s defining private-law and civil-law-notary preparation.
cases.audit_scope: External-programme identity, defining curriculum, credit/choice reconstruction and source context; no independent UCR feasibility assessment
cases.audit_basis: Notarial Law wrongly joins revised-cohort years 1/2 to year 3 expressly reserved for entrants in 2024 or earlier. The revised third year is deferred to the 2027–2028 guide. Current first/second years verify 60 each, including one restricted technology/law choice and genuine 10-EC open space. The active target and prior rc-0042 lifecycle interpretation remain supported.
cases.recommended_fix: Replace the complete mixed-cohort 180 claim with verified new-cohort 120 and an unresolved new third year. Preserve outgoing 50/5/5 only as historical context. Keep optional 10 generic with approval/level constraints, instantiate the bound technology/law slot, and retain zero-credit LLP formation separately.
cases.unresolved_factual_question: Obtain the revised third-year curriculum from the 2027–2028 guide. Verify current full/part-time pacing from applicable regulations without treating a future offering end date as current programme closure.
cases.ucr_side_assessment_note: Existing UCR claims are preserved as provenance only; no independent UCR fit conclusion is drawn. Registry/current-cohort prerequisites must be resolved before any later UCR comparison.
cases.governing_rule: First-stage exception audit scope; Production Instructions §4.4

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The complete 180-EC comparator progresses from a 60-EC general legal foundation to 60 EC combining obligations, property, family, company, administrative and European law, and then to 60 EC dominated by matrimonial property, succession, notarial corporate structures, civil procedure, real-estate law, a notarial moot court and thesis. The public programme description likewise identifies real-estate, company, matrimonial-property and inheritance law as the third-year core. No route is selected.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current official 2026–27 study product accounts for 180 EC across three 60-EC years. Year one consists of twelve 5-EC legal foundations; the zero-credit Leiden Law Practices items are omitted. Year two contains 45 EC compulsory law and business, a 5-EC restricted technology/law choice and 10 EC of programme optional subjects. Philosophy of Technology and Law is selected by official listing order. Year three contains 50 EC compulsory notarial/private-law study, one 5-EC notarial optional subject and a 5-EC thesis. The catalogue gives the programme optional subjects as placeholders rather than named choices, so they are represented transparently at group level. No formal route is selected.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall-2026-cohort availability. UCR offers GOSGATE102 Law, Society & Justice; GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy; GOSLAWJ211 Criminal Law & Criminal Justice; GOSLAWJ212 Introduction to Public International Law; GOSLAWJ213 Comparative Constitutional Law; GOSLAWJ311 Principles of Private Law; GOSLAWJ312 Foundations of European Union Law; and BENBUSI311 Transnational Business Law. GOSLAWJ311 covers general obligations, tort and contract, and GOSGATE102 introduces property law, but there is no sequence in Dutch civil property law, conveyancing, real-estate law, matrimonial property, inheritance, family law, notarial company structures, tax law, civil procedure or notarial practice. Business and political-science courses can supply context, but cannot make 23 non-PPD courses substantively relevant to civil-law notarial training.
provenance.crosswalk_check: Canonical provider, normalized registry, source-row and offering-ID sets agree; the current stored target is in scope. This set reconciliation does not itself verify its lifecycle/language attributes.
provenance.normalization_decision_check: Fresh rc-0042 resolved12September2026 retains the active180 full/part-time target and treats future delivery end dates as offering lifecycle, not programme closure. Current revised degree corroborates active identity. Current product is the ordinary full-time template; fresh formal part-time pacing was not obtained, so no mode removal is proposed.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The supported unique curriculum totals 160 EC. Its established subject identity is nevertheless clear: Ancient Near Eastern history, written sources and languages; Hebrew and Aramaic cultural history; Egyptian material culture; Levantine archaeology; Mesopotamian religion; papyrology; heritage and museology; broader ancient Mediterranean study; a thesis seminar and final thesis; and 30 EC open elective space. The unresolved 20 EC prevents the complete-comparator evaluation required before deciding whether UCR can supply a defensible 24-course match. Revisit the UCR comparison after Leiden corrects the repeated modules or publishes distinct replacements.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current 2026–27 Leiden study product assigns 60 EC to each of three years for The Ancient Near Eastern World route. It displays 180 EC, but four identical module codes recur in different years: Seminar History of the Ancient Near East (5532VGONOY), From Aram to Tel Aviv (5531VATY), Material Culture of Ancient Egypt (5531VMCEY), and History of the Modern Middle East (5851VHMMEY). A student cannot earn the same module twice. After selecting the first-listed 10-EC second-year Ancient History option and counting each module code once, the published route supports only 160 unique EC. The route page and programme regulations do not identify distinct replacements for the repeated 20 EC.

Leiden's transition is material rather than a minor catalogue omission: both former Dutch-taught specialisations are being phased out, and no official source currently identifies the remaining 120 EC for a 2026 entrant in National and International Politics. Revisit the comparison when Leiden publishes the route's second- and third-year requirements.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: Leiden introduced National and International Politics for students entering in 2026–27 and is phasing out the former Political Science and International Politics specialisations. The current study product and the 2026–27 programme-specific regulations define only the new route's 60-EC first year. The same regulations give second- and third-year curricula only for legacy students who entered the outgoing Political Science or International Politics specialisations by 2025–26. Combining the new first year with either legacy continuation would invent an unconfirmed entrant pathway. The published 60 EC consists of ten current credit-bearing first-year components; zero-credit mentorship, tutoring, study-advice and career-information items are omitted.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The supported structure is 150 EC of compulsory legal study plus 30 EC of approved free-choice space. The compulsory programme is centred on Dutch positive law—private law and civil procedure, criminal law and criminal procedure, constitutional and administrative law and procedure—together with international and European law, legal history and philosophy, research methodology, legal writing and oral argumentation, and a bachelor thesis. The remaining problem is not the degree total or field identity but the absence of one complete current-entry course sequence during the staged redesign. Revisit when Leiden publishes the revised third year.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: Leiden began a cohort-by-cohort revision of the Law bachelor in 2025–2026. The transition guide states that only the new first year was introduced for that cohort, while later years continued under the outgoing structure. For 2026–2027 the revised programme is still being phased in: current sources establish the 180-EC degree, the 150-EC compulsory/30-EC free-choice architecture, its Dutch-law learning outcomes and the published current-year course offer, but they do not provide a complete course-level three-year pathway for a student entering in 2026 without combining revised-cohort and outgoing-cohort curricula. The aggregate components below retain only the credit structure directly supported by the regulations.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The supported revised first year introduces Religious Studies; Islam, Hindu religions, Christianity and religions of antiquity; religion in a global comparative frame; anthropology of religion; source-, object- and text-based research; qualitative field research; and the faculty digital-humanities core. The official programme description confirms that later study is intended to extend research training through psychology, sociology, comparative work, electives and a bachelor thesis, but the current sources do not yet specify the remaining 120 EC for the 2026 entrant cohort. Revisit when Leiden publishes the revised second and third years.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: Leiden changed the Religious Studies curriculum from 1 September 2026. The current study guide and programme-specific regulations establish the revised 60-EC first year for students entering in 2026-2027. The displayed second year is explicitly for students who entered in 2025-2026, and the published third year belongs to the earlier curriculum sequence. The regulations' transitional provisions likewise specify a second-year programme for students who entered in 2025-2026 or earlier. Combining the new first year with those transition-cohort later years would invent an unconfirmed pathway. The supported current-entry components below therefore retain only the published revised first year.

verified_module_credit_evidence.name: Scriptieseminar Religiewetenschappen
prerequisites:
Om een bachelorscriptie Religiewetenschappen te schrijven, moet de student de propedeuse en het tweede jaar hebben afgerond. Eventuele uitzonderingen kunnen alleen worden gemaakt na overleg met de studieadviseur en de examencommissie. Het seminar staat uitsluitend open voor studenten die staan ingeschreven voor de BA Religiewetenschappen.

Naast de docent van het seminar treden andere docenten die aan het Leids Centrum voor Religiewetenschap (LUCSoR) verbonden zijn, op als individuele scriptiebegeleiders. De keuze van een begeleider hangt af van het onderwerp van de scriptie van de student en dient te worden goedgekeurd door de examencommissie. Begeleiding is dus deels collectief (wat de ‘technische’ en algemene kant van het scriptietraject betreft), via dit scriptieseminar, en deels individueel (wat de inhoudelijke kant van het scriptieonderzoek betreft), via de begeleidende gespecialiseerde docent.

provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. GOSHIST111/211/312 provide modern, imperial and research history; GOSPOLI112/212/313 provide comparative politics, international relations and conflict; BENECON111/211/311/312 provide general economics and econometrics. MCCLITR111/112/311/312 and MCCMEDI111/211 offer general literary and media analysis, while HCBCOGN312 studies psycholinguistics rather than Russian. cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden's Astronomy bachelor requires a continuous mathematical and physical foundation, dedicated astrophysics and planetary-systems study, practical observing and laboratory work, quantum mechanics, electrodynamics, stellar and galactic astrophysics, cosmology, specialist astronomy electives and a 22-EC independent astronomy research project. UCR offers useful mathematics, programming and data-science courses, but no astronomy or astrophysics course, no classical or quantum physics sequence, no astronomical observing course and no physics or astronomy laboratory. A 24-course response assembled from mathematics, computing, earth science and general natural science would replace Astronomy with adjacent tools and topics rather than implement its academic core.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The current official 2026-27 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC: a 60-EC compulsory first year; a 60-EC compulsory second year; and a third year containing 8 EC of required Radiative Processes and research integrity, a 22-EC bachelor research project, and a coherent instantiated 30-EC astronomy-centred elective package. The programme has no named graduation route. Its identity is a cumulative theory-observation-computation-research progression in astronomy, astrophysics, mathematics and physics.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current 2026-27 Leiden Study Guide and public product API define a 180-EC Astronomy bachelor with 60 EC of compulsory courses in each of years one and two. Year three contains 8 EC of further compulsory astronomy and research-skills study, a 22-EC bachelor research project, and 30 EC of restricted elective space. To instantiate that space as one broad astronomy-centred pathway, the selection combines Astro-Particle Physics, Astrobiology, Astronomy from Space, Astronomical Relativity, Bayesian Statistics for Astrophysics, Mathematical Methods of Physics and Relativistic Electrodynamics. These options cover astronomical phenomena, theory and quantitative methods, total exactly 30 EC, and were selected from the official list independently of UCR fit. All components together account for exactly 180 EC.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide mathematical tools; DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming and the data-science sequence provide computational methods. ENSENVI111 Dynamic Earth addresses geology and geophysics, while other natural-science courses concern biology, chemistry, sustainability or engineering applications. The workbook contains no course in astronomy, astrophysics, planetary systems, classical mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum mechanics, statistical physics or cosmology, and no astronomical observing or physics-laboratory sequence. The adjacent mathematical and computational courses cannot give 23 non-PPD courses a concrete Astronomy rationale or reproduce the external theory-to-research progression.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden's Linguistics bachelor requires a cumulative scientific language sequence in phonetics and speech sounds, phonology, syntax, morphology, sociolinguistics, historical linguistics, language typology, sign and gesture studies, fieldwork, grammatical description and language documentation, followed by specialised study and an independent linguistics thesis. UCR offers one dedicated Psycholinguistics course and several useful courses in rhetoric, communication, cognition, sociology, programming and data science, but it does not offer the structural-linguistics foundations or the descriptive and documentary sequence needed to organise 23 non-PPD courses around Linguistics. A 24-course response would replace the field's disciplinary core with adjacent communication, psychology and computing subjects.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The official 2026-27 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC through a 60-EC first year, a 60-EC Descriptive Linguistics second year and a third year containing 20 EC of track requirements, a 10-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC of open elective space. The selected route follows the neutral official-order rule and was reconstructed before considering UCR provision.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current 2026-27 Leiden Study Guide and public product API define 60 EC in each year. The generic Linguistics target requires one of four formal specialisations from year two. Descriptive Linguistics is the first specialisation listed on the current official programme page and is therefore selected as the neutral official-order tie-break, independently of UCR fit. Year one combines 25 EC compulsory study, the complete 25-EC English-language course set and the 10-EC Descriptive Linguistics preparation package. Year two contains the published 45-EC Descriptive Linguistics compulsory sequence plus 15 EC of restricted track electives. Year three preserves the official 20-EC Descriptive Linguistics specialisation requirement, the 10-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC of genuine elective space. The components account for exactly 180 EC.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics directly addresses language processing and cognition, while HCBGATE102 Introduction to Brain & Behavior and the cognitive-science sequence provide adjacent brain and behaviour study. MCCCOMM111 The Art of Rhetorical Communication, MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning, MCCCOMM213 Rhetoric in Action, MCCCOMM311 Persuasive Communication and MCCCOMM312 Creative Communication Laboratory address rhetoric, discourse and communication rather than linguistic structure. MCCCOMM112 Dutch is practical language learning. Sociology, anthropology, programming, AI and data-science courses add adjacent social or computational tools, but the workbook contains no course sequence in phonetics, phonology, syntax, morphology, semantics, historical linguistics, typology, linguistic fieldwork, grammatical description or language documentation. These gaps prevent a defensible 24-course Linguistics programme rather than merely limiting a specialist elective.

secondary_findings.stored: The current 2026-27 Leiden Study Guide and public product API define 60 EC in each year. The generic Linguistics target requires one of four formal specialisations from year two. Descriptive Linguistics is the first specialisation listed on the current official programme page and is therefore selected as the neutral official-order tie-break, independently of UCR fit. Year one combines 25 EC compulsory study, the complete 25-EC English-language course set and the 10-EC Descriptive Linguistics preparation package. Year two contains the published 45-EC Descriptive Linguistics compulsory sequence plus 15 EC of restricted track electives. Year three preserves the official 20-EC Descriptive Linguistics specialisation requirement, the 10-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC of genuine elective space. The components account for exactly 180 EC.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Leiden's Mathematics bachelor requires a cumulative proof-based sequence in mathematical structures, two courses each in analysis, linear algebra and algebra, followed by topology, complex function theory, measure theory, differential equations, probability and mathematical statistics, numerical mathematics, restricted advanced mathematics and an 18-EC independent mathematics project. UCR offers a useful but small applied mathematics and computing set. It has no course sequence in proof-based real analysis, abstract algebra, topology, measure theory, complex function theory or geometry and no independent mathematics research project. A 24-course response would therefore replace most of the degree's disciplinary core with computing, data science and adjacent applications.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The current official 2026-27 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC through a 60-EC first year, a 60-EC second year and a 60-EC third year. Restricted choices were instantiated by neutral official order before UCR provision was considered. The resulting route retains 36 EC of genuine open elective space and still contains a continuous 126-EC compulsory or restricted mathematics core plus the 18-EC bachelor project.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current 2026-27 Leiden Study Guide and public product API define 60 EC in each year. Year one contains 54 EC of compulsory mathematics and programming plus 6 EC of open elective space. Year two contains a 48-EC compulsory sequence and 12 EC selected from the published restricted electives; Algebra 2 and Discrete Operations Research are selected as the first two options in official order. Year three contains 12 EC of restricted mathematics study, an 18-EC bachelor project and 30 EC of open elective space. Because Algebra 2 and Discrete Operations Research were already used in year two, Algebraic Curves and Applied & Industrial Mathematics Seminar are the first two non-duplicative year-three options in official order. The choices were fixed independently of UCR fit, and all components account for exactly 180 EC.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide applied calculus, linear algebra, numerical, systems and probability tools. DISARIN212 Logic & Discrete Mathematics adds formal and discrete reasoning, while DISARIN311 Optimization Methods in AI provides an adjacent optimisation application. The workbook contains no sustained proof-based analysis or algebra sequence, topology, measure theory, complex function theory, projective or differential geometry, number theory, stochastic-process sequence or mathematics bachelor project. Programming and data-science courses are useful tools but cannot turn the remaining 15 or more non-PPD slots into a coherent Mathematics degree or reproduce the external proof-to-research progression.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Twente's Civil Engineering bachelor integrates calculus and programming with three successive structural-mechanics courses, two fluid-mechanics courses, soil mechanics, fluid measurements, construction design, water systems, transport engineering, spatial development, civil-engineering simulation and large domain projects before a 30-EC civil-engineering graduation phase. UCR offers strong environmental-sustainability, water, earth-science and spatial-planning courses and several useful mathematical and computational tools, but it does not offer the structural, materials, geotechnical, hydraulic, transport or construction-engineering sequence on which the degree's projects depend. cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The Amsterdam VU-UT Mechanical Engineering bachelor builds four compulsory semesters around mechanics of materials, manufacturing and metals; thermodynamics and renewable-energy engineering; mass manufacturing, polymers, tribology, dynamics and vibrations; and systems, signal, control, precision and finite-element engineering. Its final compulsory semester then adds fluid mechanics, heat transfer, aerodynamic wind-tunnel work and an individual mechanical-engineering research assignment. UCR offers adjacent mathematics, computing, product-design and sustainability courses, but not this mechanical-science core or its laboratory, workshop, prototype, manufacturing and engineering-research progression. A 24-course response would not preserve the programme's academic identity as Mechanical Engineering.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The current official Amsterdam curriculum accounts for the 180-EC UT degree through six 30-EC semesters. Semesters one through four provide the compulsory mechanical-engineering sequence, semester five is genuine open minor space, and semester six is compulsory scientific research in mechanical engineering. This Amsterdam location has its own semester themes and course sequence rather than simply reproducing the Enschede modules, and it has no named graduation route requiring selection.
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current VU Amsterdam curriculum defines the location-specific joint VU-UT programme as six consecutive semesters and lists the complete disciplinary content of each semester. VU states that most teaching is in Amsterdam with recurring laboratory work in Enschede; students enrol at the University of Twente for the UT Mechanical Engineering degree. The official UT current-student curriculum establishes that the three-year Mechanical Engineering bachelor totals 180 EC, or 60 EC per year. The six official semester blocks are therefore recorded at 30 EC each, preserving all 180 EC and the genuine open minor semester without inventing course-level weights that VU does not publish on the page.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant quantitative tools, while DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming adds computing. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design covers customer-needs analysis, fabrication planning and prototyping; ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design address environmental impact and sustainable-energy assessment. The workbook contains no statics, mechanics-of-materials or elasticity course; no thermodynamics, fluid-mechanics or heat-transfer sequence; no metals, polymers, manufacturing, tribology, dynamics, vibration, precision-mechanism, control-engineering or finite-element course; and no mechanical-engineering laboratory, workshop, wind-tunnel, integrated design-project or graduation-research sequence. Linear Systems is a useful adjacent signals-and-systems course, but one such course cannot substitute for the semester-scale mechatronics and mechanical-design progression.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The supported 240-EC current pathway combines primary-school subject knowledge and didactics, educational and developmental science, research methods, classroom-based inquiry and continuous school practice. School placement begins in year one, practice accounts for 25% of the programme, and the fourth year includes school-organisation study, thesis research and the final teaching placement. cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Utrecht's Veterinary Medicine bachelor is a tightly integrated professional sequence in species-specific anatomy, embryology, physiology, pharmacology, infection and immunity, organ-system disease, animal nutrition, reproduction and obstetrics, veterinary public health, clinical diagnostics, anaesthesiology, surgery and animal-population epidemiology. Two longitudinal lines progressively develop veterinary clinical reasoning, practical skills and professional judgement, including practical work with living and dead animals, tissues and anatomical models. UCR offers valuable general biomedical, life-science, ecology, ethics and public-health courses, but it does not provide the species-specific veterinary science, clinical animal examination and treatment, surgery, reproduction, nutrition, animal-patient practicals or longitudinal veterinary clinician training on which the degree depends. A 24-course response would be a human-biomedical and ecology programme with animal-related context, not Veterinary Medicine.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The official current curriculum accounts for the complete three-year, 180-EC bachelor as three 60-EC years. Year one moves from mammalian and avian anatomy and embryology through molecular and cell biology, genetics, pharmacology, physiology, infection, immunity, haematology, circulation and respiration. Year two covers organ systems, nutrition across animal species, neurology, anaesthesiology, adaptation and welfare, plus 15 EC of open electives. Year three adds reproduction and obstetrics, veterinary public health and food safety, locomotion and clinical diagnostics, animal-population epidemiology and economics, a thesis, cross-organ disorders, surgery and 7.5 EC of open electives. Veterinaire clinicus and Veterinaire professional run through all three years; there is no named bachelor specialisation requiring route selection.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: Current curriculum; checked 2026-09-27
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The official programme page defines a three-year full-time BSc and provides the complete curriculum by year and block. It also states that the first year comprises 60 EC. The 180-EC architecture is therefore recorded as three 60-EC years, retaining the named courses, the two longitudinal veterinary learning lines, the bachelor thesis and the genuine 22.5-EC elective space without inventing individual credit values that the public page does not publish. The two longitudinal lines develop throughout all three years and are represented within each year rather than double-counted as separate credits.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease provide a substantial general and human-biomedical base. HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics and HCBCOGN112 Neurobiology add population health, pathology, genetics and comparative-anatomy context. ENSECOL111 Introduction to Biodiversity, ENSECOL212 Ecosystems Uncovered, ENSECOL311 Marine Biology, ENSECOL312 Sustainable Farming & Innovation and GOSPHIL212 Ethics contribute ecology, animal biology, livestock systems, welfare-adjacent and animal-rights perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no comparative veterinary anatomy and organ-system sequence across mammal and bird species; no veterinary pharmacotherapy, diagnostics, anaesthesiology or surgery; no animal reproduction, obstetrics or species-specific nutrition; no food-production veterinary public-health training; and no practical progression with animal patients or longitudinal veterinary-clinician line. These are compulsory programme-wide gaps, not optional route differences.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Utrecht's Pharmacy bachelor is a cumulative medicines-specific programme spanning pharmaceutical chemistry, dosage forms and administration, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, pharmacotherapy, drug research, product care, biological medicines and applied treatment across infection, neurology, hormonal disease, dermatology, psychiatry, cardiovascular disease, autoimmunity and oncology. Its longitudinal academic-skills requirements and bachelor thesis are developed within this pharmaceutical sequence. UCR offers a valuable general biomedical pathway and one dedicated Pharmacology course, but it does not offer pharmaceutical chemistry, drug formulation and product care, pharmacokinetics, dosage calculation and administration, clinical medication use and safety, or a sustained disease-specific pharmacotherapy sequence. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be a biomedical-sciences programme with one pharmacology course, not Pharmacy.

The major comprises seven first-year medicines courses, ten advanced thematic pharmacy courses and a 7.5-EC bachelor thesis, with Academische Vaardigheden running longitudinally across all three years. The advanced curriculum is concentrically organised and applies prerequisites from first-year pharmacy study and specific level-2 courses to level-3 pharmacy courses.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current student curriculum explicitly defines a 180-EC bachelor with the Farmacie study path comprising 135 EC of compulsory major study and 45 EC of genuine profiling space. The compulsory list contains seven 7.5-EC first-year pharmacy courses, ten 7.5-EC advanced thematic courses and the 7.5-EC bachelor thesis option, totalling 135 EC. The longitudinal Academische Vaardigheden requirements in years one to three are embedded requirements without separately listed EC and are therefore described in the curriculum context rather than double-counted. The 15-EC thesis option would increase the major beyond the published 135 EC, so the coherent standard pathway uses the listed 7.5-EC thesis option. The target itself is the named Farmacie path rather than the separate Farmaceutische Wetenschappen path.

HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology directly studies drug targets, therapeutic use and toxicity; HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease add advanced biomedical applications. cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Utrecht's Medicine bachelor integrates organ-system biomedical science with compulsory clinical reasoning, practical clinical skills, workplace learning, patient and community experience, professional behaviour, complex-care challenges, pharmacotherapy, longitudinal interdisciplinary formation and a medical research thesis. UCR can build a strong biomedical and health-sciences programme, but it does not offer patient interviewing and physical examination, clinical skills assessment, supervised workplace learning in health-care settings, integrated diagnostic reasoning, longitudinal medical-professional formation or organ-system clinical teaching across circulation, respiration, neurology, psychiatry, digestion, urogenital and hormonal medicine, movement, lifespan care, haematology and oncology. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be biomedical science with psychology and public health, not a defensible Medicine curriculum.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The adopted 2026–27 DNUA curriculum accounts for all 180 EC through a compulsory 165-EC Medicine major and 15 EC of approved profile space. The major combines integrated biomedical and organ-system courses, four compulsory health/innovation/community carousels, three years of Discipline Overstijgend Onderwijs and Praktisch Lijnonderwijs, two years of Clinical Reasoning, Year-3 workplace learning, complex clinical care, Health Humanities, Haematology & Oncology, Pharmacology & Pharmacotherapy, the interuniversity medical progress test, and a 13-EC Science & Bachelor Thesis component.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: 2026–27 entry curriculum; checked 2026-09-28
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The adopted 2026–27 Medicine EER applies to the first entering cohort of the new De Nieuwe Utrechtse Arts curriculum and establishes a 180-EC bachelor comprising a 165-EC compulsory Medicine major and 15 EC of genuine profile space. Appendix 1b gives the complete DNUA major. The four 3-EC carousel courses are all compulsory: three are taken in Year 1 and one in Year 2, with order depending on group allocation. The EER is used for exact credits where the current student overview remains provisional: Bewegen & Waarnemen and Levensloop are each 10 EC in the adopted EER, not the earlier 9.5-EC webpage figures. The 15-EC profile space is preserved generically rather than filled with invented electives. All 180 EC are thereby accounted for.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide substantial life-science foundations. HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease provide advanced biomedical content; HCBGATE102 Introduction to Brain & Behavior, HCBCOGN112 Neurobiology and Psychology courses cover brain, behaviour and mental-health perspectives; HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health and ethics, sociology and communication courses add population, societal and ethical perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no clinical-skills or physical-examination course, no patient-interviewing sequence, no supervised clinical or workplace-learning component, no integrated diagnostic-reasoning progression, no longitudinal medical professional-behaviour curriculum, and no comprehensive clinical organ-system sequence. These compulsory programme-wide medical gaps cannot be repaired by selecting adjacent biomedical, psychology or public-health courses.

The current prospective-student curriculum identifies eight named first-year courses arranged as two four-course foundation packages, three named depth-package options, one-third free-choice space, a research seminar and a final project. The current student curriculum for the 2025-entry predecessor confirms the architecture of 60 EC in two foundation packages, a 30-EC depth package, 15 EC in two compulsory courses, 15 EC for the research seminar and final project, and 60 EC of profiling space. However, Utrecht explicitly states that it is still developing the course package for the renamed programme and that content is missing. The current page does not identify the two compulsory 15-EC major courses for new entrants, does not provide a complete credit-bearing 180-EC curriculum, and lists five items under the four-course Politics and Religion package, including two items both labelled Block 3. Combining the predecessor's unnamed requirements with the incomplete new page would therefore require guessing. The supported components below retain only the architecture and named current elements that can be established without inventing the missing 15 EC.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Utrecht Chemistry is defined by a compulsory first-year sequence in organic chemistry and spectroscopy, physical and inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, quantum chemistry, mathematics and physics, with extensive laboratory work. The selected Molecules and Materials pathway continues through physical, inorganic, solid-state, electrochemical, structural, spectroscopic, catalytic, organometallic, polymer, nano- and surface chemistry and ends in an individual chemistry research project. UCR has no chemistry gateway and no stand-alone progression in organic, inorganic, analytical, physical, quantum or synthetic chemistry. A 24-course UCR programme could combine biochemistry, environmental science, sustainability, mathematics and programming, but it would omit the target’s defining chemistry theory and multi-laboratory spine and would therefore misrepresent the degree.

cases.audit_basis: Current Chemistry OER specifies compulsory82.5 including Biochemical Methods/Academic Formation2 rather than universally compulsory Inorganic/Solid-State Chemistry; restricted52.5 and free45. The stored pathway omits the mandatory Category2 Chemical Biology-or-Biochemistry2 choice and uses all180 for chemistry selections, hiding the genuine free45. Current formal level3 teaching and required Methods/thesis catalogues establish English, omitted by NLD-only metadata. The formal table has stronger level minima than the formal prose; the proposed choice satisfies both. The student page expressly applies to2025 entrants and has different minima, so it is not silently substituted for the2026 formal table.

Correct NLD + ENG. Preserve valid prerequisite-satisfied selected content where possible; replace Organometallic if its required organic/inorganic level2 formation is not retained.

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The current public curriculum and its linked visual schedule account for exactly 180 EC: eight 7.5-EC compulsory first-year courses (60 EC), fourteen selected 7.5-EC post-first-year courses (105 EC), and a 15-EC ten-week individual bachelor thesis project. The first-listed Molecules and Materials path is instantiated with courses in molecular modelling, physical and organic chemistry, compulsory inorganic/solid-state chemistry, electrochemistry, structure determination, spectroscopy, catalysis, nanomaterials, organometallic and polymer chemistry, solids and surfaces, plus biochemical research methods. The live page is current as checked on 2026-09-28; its linked visual schedule remains labelled 2025–26 and the page cautions that offerings can change.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: Current public curriculum checked 2026-09-28; linked visual schedule labelled 2025–2026
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current official curriculum page defines a three-year, 180-EC bachelor organised as four blocks of two courses per year and says the current public course list is indicative. Year one comprises eight compulsory 7.5-EC foundations (60 EC). In years two and three students choose from category-based chemistry offerings and free choices, complete the compulsory Anorganische & Vastestofchemie course and finish with a 15-EC ten-week individual bachelor research project. The generic target names neither of the two official study paths, so the first-listed Moleculen en Materialen path is selected by neutral official order. A coherent 105-EC set of fourteen 7.5-EC post-first-year courses is instantiated from the published materials, physical, inorganic, analytical and supporting-methods offerings; the 15-EC thesis completes the later 120 EC. The linked one-page visual schedule is still labelled 2025–26, while the live public curriculum page was checked on 2026-09-28 and is treated as the current source; the public page warns that offerings may change.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory provide biomolecular content and one broad biochemical/molecular laboratory course. HCBGATE101 and HCBLIFE211 cover cells and molecular life science. ENSGATE101/201 contain some general physics, chemistry and materials-science foundations; ENSENVI311 Environmental Biogeochemistry and ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation touch geochemical or inorganic processes and resource recovery; ENSSUST112 addresses life-cycle and circular-economy analysis. DISGATE102 and DISGATE101 supply mathematical and programming support. None provides a disciplinary chemistry sequence in organic synthesis, inorganic and solid-state chemistry, analytical measurement, thermodynamics and physical chemistry, quantum chemistry, molecular spectroscopy, catalysis, electrochemistry or materials characterisation, nor a progressive set of chemistry laboratories. These isolated biochemical, environmental and sustainability offerings cannot support 23 non-PPD courses with concrete relevance to a Chemistry concept or prepare a student for the target’s independent chemistry research project.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Utrecht's programme is defined by a compulsory four-course Spanish-language acquisition sequence progressing from CEFR A1 to B2, followed by Spanish-medium and Spanish-specific study of sociolinguistics, morphosyntax, language change, intercultural communication, Spanish and Latin American literature, theatre, film, migration, colonial chronicles, cultural identity and historical memory. UCR's current curriculum contains no Spanish-language course and no course whose disciplinary object is Spanish language, Hispanic linguistics, Spanish or Latin American literature, or the cultures of Spain and Latin America. UCR literature, media, history, sociology and communication courses can illuminate isolated comparative themes, but they cannot supply the language competence on which the comparator's advanced courses and thesis depend. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be a broad literature, media and cultural-studies programme without Spanish, not a defensible closest match to Spanish Language and Culture.

The major contains 60 EC of compulsory first-year foundations, including 30 EC of progressive Spanish acquisition; 45 EC of Trans-Atlantic Perspectives depth study; a 7.5-EC methods course; a 7.5-EC professional/creative/academic writing course; and a 7.5-EC bachelor thesis. provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current student curriculum explicitly applies to the 2026 entrant cohort and fixes the programme at 180 EC: a 127.5-EC major and 52.5 EC of profiling space. The major comprises two first-year foundation packages (eight courses, 60 EC); six 7.5-EC depth courses (45 EC); one 7.5-EC methods course; a 7.5-EC professional, creative and academic writing course preparing the capstone; and a 7.5-EC bachelor thesis. A Fall-2026 entrant reaches Year 2 in 2027-2028 and therefore follows the odd-year Trans-Atlantic Perspectives package (Competencias de lectura y conciencia cultural, Migration and Diaspora, Testimonios/crónicas/imágenes, and Variation and Change in Language). In Year 3, the student takes two courses from the even-year package; the first two officially listed courses, Lengua, cultura e identidad and Contesting the Past, are selected neutrally. Research Methods Intercultural Communication is the first-listed eligible methods choice. The current official page identifies Crossing Borders as an optional alternative track; the standard Trans-Atlantic Perspectives package best represents the generic normalized target's Spanish-language-and-culture identity and is selected before UCR fit is considered. The genuine 52.5-EC profiling space remains open. The resulting pathway accounts for exactly 180 EC.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. No course teaches Spanish language at any level, Spanish linguistics, Hispanic literature, or Spanish and Latin American cultural history as its sustained disciplinary object. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literature, MCCLITR112 Texts & Worlds, MCCLITR212 Literature & Society, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Contemporary Literatures offer transferable literary and cultural analysis; MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media, MCCMEDI211 Media Archaeology, MCCCOMM211 Intercultural Communication and MCCCOMM311 Persuasive Communication offer adjacent media and communication study; GOSHIST courses provide broad historical methods and selected regional themes; and GOSSOCI212 provides qualitative research. These courses could support comparative cultural work, but none develops Spanish speaking, listening, reading or writing, and none supports progression from A1 to B2 or prepares students to conduct advanced Spanish-language coursework and an independent thesis in the field. Because the missing language sequence is a prerequisite academic foundation rather than a peripheral specialty, 23 non-PPD UCR courses cannot form a coherent Spanish Language and Culture programme.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: Utrecht's ordinary Mathematics bachelor requires a cumulative proof-based core in calculus and linear algebra, analysis, abstract algebra, probability, multivariable analysis and topology, followed by restricted higher mathematics, a 15-EC mathematical thesis and additional advanced mathematical choice. UCR has a useful applied quantitative set but no proof-based sequence in analysis or abstract algebra, no topology or differential-geometry pathway, and no independent mathematics thesis. Even after using every directly relevant UCR mathematics course, most of the 23 non-PPD places in a UCR programme would have to be filled with computing, data science and applications that cannot substitute for this disciplinary progression. A 24-course alternative would therefore misrepresent the target rather than provide a defensible Mathematics programme.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The adopted 2026-2027 programme appendix defines the ordinary Bachelor Wiskunde as 180 EC: a 135-EC Mathematics major and 45 EC of profiling space. The major contains 82.5 EC compulsory study, one 7.5-EC modelling choice, 15 EC of restricted choice and 30 EC of further Mathematics choice. The compulsory sequence includes proof, two integrated calculus-and-linear-algebra courses, analysis, groups and rings, programming, probability, multivariable analysis, topology and a 15-EC bachelor thesis. The generic normalized target does not name the separate Wiskunde & Toepassingen direction, so the ordinary Bachelor Wiskunde in Overview 1 is reconstructed and no route is selected. Where the ordinary programme requires choices, the first eligible courses in the formally adopted table order are used neutrally and independently of UCR provision: Modelling with ODEs and PDEs for the modelling choice; Discrete Mathematics and Complex Analysis for the 15-EC restricted choice; and Mathematics Lab, Multivariable Analysis, Mathematical Game Theory and Differentiable Manifolds for the 30-EC Mathematics choice. The 45-EC profiling space remains genuinely open. The public curriculum page corroborates the three-year structure, eight-course first year, mathematical subject progression, 45 EC of wholly free choice and the distinction between ordinary Mathematics study paths and the separate Mathematics & Applications direction.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods supplies applied calculus and linear-algebra tools; DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide valuable applied mathematical progression. DISARIN212 Logic & Discrete Mathematics adds formal and discrete reasoning, and DISARIN311 Optimization Methods in AI is a relevant application. The workbook does not contain a sustained proof-based real-analysis sequence, abstract algebra beyond introductory discrete material, topology, complex analysis, differentiable manifolds or a mathematics bachelor-thesis course. Programming, data-science, econometrics and AI courses support mathematical applications but cannot supply the missing disciplinary core or turn the remaining non-PPD course slots into a coherent Mathematics degree.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The UvA programme is defined by cumulative French-language acquisition and French-medium study. It develops speaking, listening, reading and writing through six compulsory language modules, integrates that competence with French linguistics, literature, cinema, culture and society, requires a 30-EC semester at a university in a French-speaking country, and culminates in a French research workshop and graduation project. UCR's current catalogue contains no French-language course at any level and no sustained sequence in French linguistics or French-language literature. UCR literature, media, history, politics and cultural-analysis courses can illuminate isolated comparative questions, but they cannot supply the French competence on which the study-abroad semester and advanced disciplinary work depend. A 24-course response would therefore be a broad European humanities and social-science programme without French, not a defensible closest match to French Language and Culture.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current official UvA curriculum, checked 2026-09-29, defines a complete 180-EC pathway with 60 EC in each year and no formal route. Year 2 contains French literature, French linguistics, a fifth language-acquisition module, philosophy of science, French cinema and a compulsory 30-EC semester in a French-speaking country. Year 3 contains a sixth French-language module, European literature, a French research workshop, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC graduation project. provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows with course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. No course teaches French speaking, listening, reading, writing, grammar or translation, and no course provides French linguistics or French-language literary study as its sustained disciplinary object. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature, MCCLITR212 Life & Travel Writing, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide transferable literary and cultural analysis; MCCMEDI courses support film and media analysis; GOSHIST, GOSPOLI and GOSECON courses support historical, political and economic comparison; and HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics examines language processing and acquisition generally. These courses could support comparative study of European culture, politics, history and representation, but they do not develop French proficiency or prepare students for French-medium coursework, a semester at a university in a French-speaking country and an independent graduation project grounded in French language and culture. Because the missing language sequence is the programme's academic foundation rather than a peripheral specialty, 23 non-PPD UCR courses cannot form a coherent French Language and Culture programme.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The UvA Medicine bachelor is an integrated, patient-centred medical programme. Four recurring organ-system themes are taught through disease cases; clinical lectures include real patients from the first year; students complete a compulsory observation and care placement; and medical-technical and medical-communication skills, history-taking, physical examination, clinical reasoning, academic formation and professional development progress across all three years. The 14-EC final practice block explicitly prepares students for medical clerkships. UCR can build a strong biomedical and health-sciences programme, but it cannot reproduce the compulsory patient-facing placement, longitudinal clinical-skills training, supervised medical communication and examination, integrated diagnostic reasoning or medical professional formation. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be biomedical science with psychology and public health, not a defensible Medicine programme.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current official UvA curriculum, checked 2026-09-29, defines one complete 180-EC Medicine pathway with 60 EC in each year and no formal route. Year 1 combines four patient-centred organ-system themes, a 6-EC observation and care placement, clinical and scientific methodology, academic formation and professional development. Year 2 deepens the same themes and longitudinal formation while preserving 18 EC of genuine elective space. Year 3 continues the themes and formation, includes a 12-EC medical bachelor thesis and culminates in a 14-EC preparation-for-practice block focused on clinical reasoning, history-taking and physical examination before clerkships. The official overview confirms the normalized identity, three-year 180-EC load, Dutch language, Amsterdam UMC location and RIO code 56551. Elective space is preserved without invented content.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide substantial life-science foundations. HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease provide advanced biomedical content. HCBGATE102 Introduction to Brain & Behavior, HCBCOGN112 Neurobiology and UCR psychology courses cover brain, behaviour and mental-health perspectives; HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health and ethics, sociology, communication and research-methods courses add population, societal, ethical and scientific perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no patient-facing clinical placement, no history-taking or physical-examination course, no longitudinal medical-technical and medical-communication skills strand, no integrated diagnostic-reasoning progression, no supervised medical professional-development curriculum, and no preparation for clinical clerkships. These compulsory programme-wide clinical gaps cannot be repaired by selecting adjacent biomedical, psychology, public-health or communication courses.

MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology and MCCHEAM213 Greek Archaeology cover ancient material culture; MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy treats Athenian civic heritage; MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature discusses Homer and Virgil alongside other traditions; MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy and MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean offer adjacent historical, philosophical or literary context. These support ancient-world inquiry, but none teaches Ancient Greek or Latin grammar, translation, close reading in the original languages, or a progressive classical philology sequence. Communications courses such as MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning address language in other contexts and cannot substitute. Even a coherent archaeology-and-literature 24-course plan would miss the external degree’s defining language core.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The defining curriculum begins with compulsory general music theory, two successive solfège and harmony/analysis courses, score reading and analysis, four chronological Western music-history courses, cultural musicology, music cognition and academic study of musical cultures. It then requires music ethnography, popular-music studies, quantitative musicology, philosophy and research projects, specialization work in computational and cognitive musicology and rhythm, and an independent musicology thesis. The current UCR catalogue has no course in music theory, solfège, harmony, score analysis, music history, ethnomusicology or musicology research methods, and no sustained music-cognition sequence. A 24-course programme assembled from general film, media, literature, art history, cognition, sociology and computing would replace the target’s central object of study and disciplinary progression rather than provide a defensible closest match. Even the 42 EC of genuinely open choice cannot compensate for the absent compulsory musicological core.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The official common curriculum and 2026–27 study guide reconcile to an exact 60+60+60=180 EC full-time pathway. The normalized target names no specialization, so the first-listed Cognitive and Computational Musicology route is selected under the neutral official-order rule. Year 1 is a 60-EC foundation in musicology, Western music history, cultural musicology, cognition, music theory, solfège, harmony, repertoire and Music and AI. The selected year-2 programme consists of 48 EC of common methods, analysis, philosophy and research work plus 12 EC of route courses. Year 3 combines a 6-EC route course with the published 6-EC programme-bound choice, 36 EC open choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The public schedule displays common choice slots while the study guide supplies route content; alternatives are not added together. The same curriculum can be taken part-time over six years, but this reconstruction uses the standard full-time structure.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites, planned terms and topics. GOSHIST311 Native American Histories includes Indigenous music within one historical topic; MCCCOMM312 Creative Communication Laboratory may use sonic poetry while explicitly not constituting music performance or songwriting; MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media can address sound as part of audiovisual form; MCCHEAM111 Introduction to Western Art History supplies broad cultural history; HCBCOGN311 Higher Order Functions and HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics provide adjacent cognitive study; and DISARIN311 Optimization Methods in AI supplies computational methods. These are isolated encounters or neighbouring disciplines. None teaches notation, ear training, harmony, score analysis, historical repertoires, ethnomusicological fieldwork, systematic music cognition or musicology research as a coherent sequence. The workbook therefore provides no defensible basis for a scheduled 24-course UCR Musicology programme.

cases.programme_display_name: Modern Greek Language and Culture (Nieuwgriekse taal en cultuur)
cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The defining curriculum requires four successive Modern Greek language-acquisition courses in year 1, two advanced Modern Greek language-and-literature courses in year 2, further Greek-language acquisition during a required semester in Greece or Cyprus, Greek-language source use, and a Modern Greek subject thesis. This language progression is integrated with Byzantine legacies, modern Greek and Cypriot history, Greece-Turkey-Cyprus conflict and memory, Greek-European relations and contemporary Mediterranean culture. The current UCR catalogue has no Modern Greek language instruction, Greek grammar or translation, or advanced Greek-language reading and writing sequence. A 24-course programme assembled from ancient Greek archaeology, general literature, history, politics, philosophy and Mediterranean art would replace the programme's compulsory modern-language and area-studies core rather than provide a defensible closest match. The 30 EC of genuine open choice cannot compensate for the missing compulsory Modern Greek sequence and country-specific progression.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The official programme is 60+60+60=180 EC. Year 1 lists nine compulsory components totaling 60 EC, including four successive Modern Greek language-acquisition courses, Byzantine and modern Greek history, humanities and regional-studies foundations, and Project Athens. Year 2 contains five 6-EC UvA courses in advanced Greek language and literature, national identity, conflict and cultural history, followed by the required half-year study-abroad semester in Greece or Cyprus. The compact table labels the administrative Buitenlandverblijf component as 6 EC, while the accompanying text identifies the whole second semester as the abroad period and expects 12 EC of Modern Greek language acquisition there; the 30-EC semester is therefore preserved as one integrated abroad block without inventing host courses. Year 3 lists three 6-EC Mediterranean and Greece-Europe courses, 30 EC genuine free choice and a 12-EC thesis. This yields the coherent published 60+60+60 pathway.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites, planned terms and topics. MCCHEAM213 Greek Archaeology focuses on community and democracy in early-democratic ancient Greece; MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy examines Athenian democracy, archaeology and heritage; MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature includes ancient Greek and Byzantine narrative among a global set; GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy begins with ancient Greek philosophy; and GOSHIST213 Western Way of War ranges from Greek hoplites to the modern era. MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean, GOSHIST111 Modern History, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations and GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict provide broader historical, Mediterranean or political context. These courses concern antiquity, general regional history or adjacent methods. None teaches Modern Greek grammar, vocabulary, pronunciation, speaking, writing, translation or Greek-language source analysis, and none provides a sustained modern Greece/Cyprus area-studies sequence. The workbook therefore provides no defensible basis for a scheduled 24-course UCR Modern Greek Language and Culture programme.

cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The UvA bachelor is defined by sustained disciplinary study of Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism and Buddhism; sacred-text interpretation; lived religion; Western esotericism; religion and spirituality in the Netherlands; religious art, myth and popular culture; disciplinary history and philosophy; and two dedicated Religious Studies research projects culminating in a thesis. UCR has relevant courses in philosophy, sociology, politics, history, archaeology, literature and cultural analysis, but no course or sequence in Religious Studies, theology, comparative religion, sacred texts, lived religion or the history of religious traditions. A 24-course UCR programme could examine culture, ideas and institutions around religion, yet most courses would treat religion only incidentally and would omit the target’s defining disciplinary core. Publishing it as a closest match would therefore misstate what UCR teaches.

Year two is 60 EC of ten listed 6-EC Religious Studies components spanning religion/art/culture, Western esotericism, religion and spirituality in the Netherlands, philosophy of science, disciplinary history/philosophy, and two research projects. MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology, MCCHEAM211 African Art & Heritage, MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean, MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature include limited religious, Islamic or mythic material. provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The formally adopted 2026-2027 ACTA curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: 60 EC in each of three years, with no open elective space. It contains 33 compulsory components spanning biomedical foundations, oral biology and disease, research methods, four progressive dental-skills lines, prevention, care planning, restorative dentistry, periodontology, medically complex patients, evidence-based dentistry, a 14-EC scientific internship, endodontology, radiology, clinical treatment and professionally assessed conduct. Patient care is an explicit curriculum requirement, and access to patient treatment depends on successful preclinical practical work.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: 2026-2027 ACTA bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The 2026-2027 ACTA OER is the formally adopted source for the compulsory curriculum and confirms that ACTA is a collaboration of the University of Amsterdam and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. The official study guide confirms a three-year, 180-EC Dutch-taught bachelor. All listed units are compulsory and total 60+60+60=180 EC; there is no open elective space. Year 1 combines cells, tissues, organ systems, oral biology, cariology, microbiology, direct restorations, research methods and statistics, professional development, and two dental-skills lines. Year 2 combines prevention, care planning, immunology and pathology, cariology and periodontology, crowns, periodontitis, the medically complex patient, professional development, preparation for the scientific internship, dental prevention and two further dental-skills lines. Year 3 combines bridges, oral biology and periodontology, medically complex patients, evidence-based dentistry, a 14-EC scientific internship, endodontics, radiology, prevention/treatment and indirect-restoration clinical lines, professional development and professionally assessed conduct. The OER explicitly requires patient care and makes successful preclinical practical work a condition for treating patients.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites, planned availability, disciplines, topics and methods. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity, HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide relevant biomedical foundations. HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBPSYC211 Statistics & Experimental Methods, HCBPSYC311 Medical & Health Psychology and HCBPSYC313 Advanced Research Seminar provide public-health, behavioural and research perspectives. None of the 151 courses teaches oral anatomy or biology, cariology, periodontology, dental biomaterials, crowns or bridges, restorative technique, endodontology, dental radiology, dental care planning, preclinical operative skills or supervised treatment of dental patients. The workbook therefore provides no defensible basis for a scheduled 24-course UCR Dentistry programme.

provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The current official programme table reconstructs a complete 180-EC full-time bachelor: 60 EC in each of three years. Year 1 establishes Theatre Studies concepts and methods through dramaturgy, European and global performance history, academic skills, arts/culture/society and a 12-EC performance-analysis course. Year 2 develops theatre-text analysis, translation from text to performance, philosophy of science, Dutch theatre history in European context and a study trip, with one 6-EC programme-restricted choice and 6 EC of free choice. Year 3 combines one further 6-EC programme-restricted choice, Performing Ecocriticism, 36 EC of free choice and a 12-EC thesis. The published explanation identifies 54 EC of total choice space (12 EC programme-restricted and 42 EC free choice); those formal choice components are preserved without inventing selections. Although the overview mentions a possible internship within the graduation trajectory, the detailed curriculum states that an internship is not compulsory, so none is inserted.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites, planned availability, disciplines, topics and methods. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies includes drama as one literary genre; MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works discusses texts that have influenced theatre; MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature briefly considers storytelling in theatrical performance; MCCLITR311 Film & Text analyses film adaptation, including acting; MCCCOMM312 Creative Communication Laboratory includes poetry and performance as creative communication; and media, art-history, rhetoric and cultural-studies courses supply broader interpretive contexts. These are adjacent fragments. None provides dramaturgy, Theatre Studies concepts and methods, theatre or performance history, sustained analysis of live performance, theatre-text-to-production study or a Theatre Studies research progression. The workbook therefore provides no defensible basis for a scheduled 24-course UCR Theatre Studies programme.
