cases.existing_substantive_exception_reason: The defining common curriculum is a specialist food-science and engineering sequence: two levels of organic and general chemistry, food microbiology and chemistry, food physics and engineering, preservation, hazards, packaging, quality systems, integrated product properties and a 24-EC food-science thesis. UCR offers adjacent life-science, sustainability and general product-design courses but no food-technology, chemistry, microbiology, process-engineering, preservation, packaging or food-quality sequence. Constructing a 24-course path would therefore require extensive padding with unrelated health, business or environmental courses and would produce a different degree. The 30-EC free-choice space cannot repair the missing 150-EC common core.
cases.audit_scope: External-programme identity, defining curriculum, credit/choice reconstruction and source context; no independent UCR feasibility assessment
cases.audit_basis: The current public WUR handbook and all relevant course records corroborate the 123-EC compulsory cluster, one 3-EC mathematics option and 24-EC thesis, totalling common 150 plus genuine elective 30. The selected Mathematics Applied: Introduction is the first listed admissible option subject to prior education and study-adviser consultation; Statistics 1 is its alternative, not extra credit. General Safety and Laboratory Safety are mandatory zero-EC course descriptions despite false required flags in the programme table; the stored source notes already acknowledge both. Thesis entry is at least 102 compulsory/restricted EC including all first-year 60. English full-time 180-EC identity is supported; shared mathematics EN/NL course variants do not invalidate the English programme.
cases.recommended_fix: Retain the current positive-credit structure and recognized zero-credit safety formation. Keep mathematics selection conditional on prior preparation/adviser agreement, use the English-compatible offering, keep optional restricted cluster with minimum zero and internship within genuine electives, and retain thesis entry 102 including first-year 60. Do not stack all optional courses or add safety credits.
cases.ucr_side_assessment_note: Existing UCR claims are preserved as provenance only; no independent UCR fit conclusion is drawn. Registry/current-cohort prerequisites must be resolved before any later UCR comparison.
cases.governing_rule: First-stage exception audit scope; Production Instructions §4.4

provenance.existing_curriculum_context: The generic published programme totals 180 EC: 123 EC compulsory credited courses, 3 EC selected from a restricted mathematics choice, a compulsory 24-EC BSc Thesis Food Science and Technology, and 30 EC genuine free choice. Zero-credit General Safety and Laboratory Safety requirements are acknowledged but do not change the credit total. No specialization or elective package is fabricated.
provenance.existing_comparator_academic_year: 2026–2027 WUR study handbook, checked 2026-09-28
provenance.existing_comparator_source_notes: The official 2026 study handbook defines a 150-EC common part and 30 EC free-choice space. The common part comprises a 123-EC compulsory credited cluster, one 3-EC restricted-choice mathematics course and a compulsory 24-EC BSc thesis. Mathematics Applied: Introduction is selected from the two published 3-EC mathematics options by official order. General Safety and Laboratory Safety are zero-credit requirements and are not counted as EC-bearing components. The programme has no formal specialization route; the programme page's examples of minors describe ways to use the free-choice space rather than mutually exclusive degree routes.
provenance.existing_ucr_course_evidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, prerequisites and planned terms. HCBGATE101 Life Science: The Foundation of Life, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory provide cell-biology, biochemical and general laboratory foundations, but they do not create a food chemistry, food microbiology or food-processing sequence. ENSECOL312 Sustainable Farming & Innovation addresses agricultural production systems; ENSDELT311 Recycling, Recovery & Remediation and ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy address environmental and circular systems; BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design provides generic product-design context. DISGATE102 Research Methods & Statistics and DISMATH314 Multivariate Data Analysis provide general quantitative methods. None substitutes for the compulsory progression in general and organic chemistry, physical chemistry, food preservation, food physics and engineering, hazards, packaging, quality operations and integrated food-product properties. These isolated adjacent offerings cannot support a coherent 24-course Food Technology programme.
